2298788.title: Semiconductor and AI Revolution
2298788.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Semiconductor and AI Revolution
Powering the Future
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:47PM by PIB Delhi

Powering the Future

From Chips to AI: Building India’s Technology Leadership

Semiconductors are the foundation of modern technology, powering everything from smartphones and vehicles to satellites and AI systems. AI is now accelerating the demand for advanced chips, specialised processors and high-performance computing, making the two technologies increasingly inseparable. Recognising this convergence, India is building capabilities from chip design and fabrication to computing infrastructure and indigenous AI models. Government initiatives across both sectors are creating an integrated technology ecosystem that strengthens self-reliance, supply-chain resilience and innovation. This convergence is also opening new opportunities in advanced manufacturing, research, entrepreneurship and high-value employment. As India marks its 80th Independence Day, these capabilities mark a decisive step towards global technology leadership and a Viksit Bharat.

Semiconductors: Foundation for Technological Self-Reliance

India is building domestic capabilities across the semiconductor value chain, from chip design and fabrication to advanced packaging, equipment and materials. By strengthening domestic capabilities today, India is positioning itself to shape the technologies of tomorrow.

Dedicated Mission Laid The Foundation For Self-Reliance

  • Semicon 1.0 laid the foundation with a ₹76,000 crore outlay to build India’s semiconductor ecosystem.
  • It supports the entire value chain, spanning chip design, fabrication, packaging, testing, equipment, materials and skilled talent etc.
  • Semicon 2.0 is scaling this foundation into global ecosystem leadership, with a ₹1,27,500 crore outlay approved in July 2026.
  • Six strategic pillars drive Semicon India 2.0: chip design, semiconductor equipment and materials, fabrication facilities, advanced packaging, research and development, and talent development.

This integrated approach strengthens supply-chain resilience, expands domestic value addition and positions India for future semiconductor leadership.

From Policy to Semiconductor Manufacturing

  • 12 semiconductor projects have been approved across six states, with investments commitments exceeding ₹1.64 lakh crore.
  • Projects span silicon and compound semiconductor fabs, display fabrication and advanced packaging facilities.
  • Three facilities have already commenced commercial production, marking India’s transition from semiconductor policy to manufacturing.

Semiconductor facilities will supply critical components for automobiles, telecommunications, aerospace, power electronics and consumer electronics

  • Semiconductor fabs plants that build raw silicon wafers into functioning integrated circuits and microchips.
  • Display fabrication are Plants that build flat and flexible screens for phones, cars, and gadgets etc.
  • Advanced packaging methods that encase, wire, and shield fragile chips to make them run faster and last longer.

Developing Indigenous Semiconductor Design Capabilities

  • To meet future workforce requirements, the Government has prioritised semiconductor skilling through initiatives such as Chips to Startup (C2S), under which,
  • Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools have been deployed in 320 academic institutions and
  • Over 68,000 students trained, expanding access to advanced chip-design capabilities. Click to Read More About: Chips to Start-up (C2S) Programme
  • 24 semiconductor design projects have also been approved for financial support and 105 startups/MSMEs for EDA tool support under DLI Scheme. Click to Read More About: Design Linked Incentive Scheme

Electronic Design Automation (EDA)

EDA tools are software platforms used to design, simulate, verify and optimize semiconductor chips. They manage complex chip designs, detect errors before manufacturing, and improve performance, power efficiency and reliability. By reducing design time, costs and manufacturing risks, EDA tools enable faster development of advanced chips for various applications.

 

  • 211 chips were taped out by 75 institutions by April 2026, demonstrating growing domestic design capabilities.
  • 7 chips have been successfully fabricated at various nodes including advanced nodes such as 12 nm.
  • Semicon 2.0 will further intended to support semiconductor IP, chip and system designs, strengthening India’s position as a global semiconductor design hub.

Global Partnerships

  • Global partnerships with the United States, Japan, Singapore, the Netherlands, Germany and the European Union are strengthening technology collaboration and ecosystem development.
  • Semicon India 2025 brought together 350+ exhibitors and participants from 48 countries and regions, strengthening India’s global semiconductor engagement.
  • The event recorded 35,000 registrations, 30,000 footfalls and 25,000 online viewers, reflecting strong global interest in India’s semiconductor ambitions.
  • 12 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) were announced to strengthen product development, services and semiconductor skill development.

These partnerships are helping integrate Indian companies into global semiconductor value chains and accelerate domestic capabilities.

IndiaAI Mission: Building India’s Sovereign and Inclusive AI Ecosystem

The IndiaAI Mission, approved with an outlay of about ₹10,372 crore, has made significant strides over the past year. The Mission`s ambition is focused on building capabilities that are secure, inclusive and rooted in Indian needs. It aims to make AI a strategic capability for innovation, economic growth and public service delivery.

Sovereign AI Computing Capacity At Scale

  • The IndiaAI Mission has expanded shared compute capacity to 45,000+ Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), as of June 2026.
  • By August 2026, 237 projects had accessed subsidised AI computing, covering 93.18 lakh GPU hours. This provides affordable high-performance computing for AI model development, training, testing and research, lowering entry barriers for Indian researchers, start-ups and innovators.

 

Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)

A GPU is a specialised electronic processor designed to accelerate graphics, image processing and other data-intensive computing tasks. GPUs are widely used in computers, smartphones, servers and other digital devices.

 

Foundational AI Models

  • From 506 applications received, the Government has selected 20 indigenous foundation model proposals, including 12 Large Multimodal Models and 8 Small Language Models.
  • This strengthens India’s capabilities in developing AI models suited to Indian languages, needs and contexts.

 

Digital Backbone For AI Models

  • As of July 2026, AI Kosh hosts over 14,000 datasets and 331 AI models, providing researchers, developers and innovators access to critical resources for building and scaling AI solutions.

 

From Laboratories To Real-World Governance

  • As on Aug 2026, IndiaAI initiatives have developed 62 AI prototypes and deployed 20 AI solutions across public-sector institutions.
  • 11 national-level hackathons and innovation challenges are further expanding the pipeline from ideas to deployable solutions.

 

Innovation Via Centres Of Excellences

  • As on Aug 2026, 58 Artificial Intelligence Centres of Excellence (AI CoEs) have been approved across States and Union Territories.
  • 22 CoE already approved and initiated across 13 States/UTs.
  • These centres are strengthening domain-specific research, innovation and application development.

 

Building The Talent And Deep-Tech Ecosystem

  • The National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) has established 25 Technology Innovation Hubs across leading academic institutions.
  • These hubs support research, skills, start-ups and technology transfer across AI, robotics, cybersecurity, quantum technologies and other emerging fields.

 

Trusted AI Alongside Rapid Adoption

  • As of July 2026, the Indian government approved 13 Responsible AI projects under the Safe & Trusted AI pillar of the IndiaAI Mission. These projects tackle critical challenges like bias mitigation, machine unlearning, deepfake detection, privacy-preserving AI, explainability, and AI risk assessment.

 

Expansion of Data Centre Capacity to Support AI Infrastructure

  • Data centres are located across the country such as Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR and Gujarat.
  • The installed capacity has grown from 375 MW in 2020 to current capacity of about 1,575 MW.
  • The Data Centre industry is now further expanding in states like Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh & West Bengal which are coming up with new investment destinations.

Global Recognition

  • The Stanford Global AI Vibrancy Report 2025 ranked India third globally in AI competitiveness and ecosystem vibrancy.
  • In 2025, India was the second-largest contributor to GitHub AI projects, reflecting the strength of its developer and innovation community.
  • The India AI Impact Summit 2026 was held in February 2026. Participation from delegations from more than 100 countries and 20 international organisations, with the declaration adopted by 92 countries and organisations.
  • India joined the Pax Silica coalition at the India AI Impact Summit 2026, working with the United States and other partners to strengthen resilient global silicon supply chains.
  • This complements India’s domestic efforts to build a self-reliant, inclusive and globally competitive AI ecosystem.

Sustaining Momentum in Chips and AI

India’s semiconductor programme is progressing from approvals and design support to commercial production. The next phase, Semicon 2.0, broadens the focus to equipment, materials, advanced packaging, research, indigenous intellectual property and talent. The IndiaAI Mission is building shared compute and supporting applications across government, industry, academia and start-ups. This integrated approach is strengthening technology capabilities, enabling responsible AI governance and supporting sustained innovation.

2298778.title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: iGOT MISSION KARMAYOGI IN WEST BENGAL
2298778.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2298778.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: iGOT MISSION KARMAYOGI IN WEST BENGAL
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:24PM by PIB Delhi

Presently 90,276 civil servants from West Bengal have been onboarded on the iGOT Karmayogi platform. The Government of West Bengal has not yet signed the tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) under Mission Karmayogi.

So far, eight draft Capacity Building Plans (CBPs) have been prepared for Government of West Bengal's priority departments. The iGOT Karmayogi digital learning platform hosts over 5,600 courses covering domain, functional and behavioural competencies. These courses are available for consumption for all registered users including those from West Bengal. As on date, 10,493 course completions have been recorded by learners from West Bengal. Further, all employees of the Central Government and officers of the All India Services, including those serving in West Bengal have to mandatorily complete prescribed courses annually on iGOT which gets reflected in their respective APARs for the corresponding period.

The DoPT, along with the other implementing agencies of Mission Karmayogi – Capacity Building Commission (CBC), and SPV Karmayogi Bharat (KB) are supporting the Government of West Bengal in its capacity building initiatives including handholding for the adoption of the role-based competency framework, onboarding on the iGOT platform, and integrating iGOT with other HR platforms/tools. A Programme Coordinator from CBC and an Assistant Manager from KB serve as Nodal Officers for the state of West Bengal for this purpose. DoPT also supports targeted capacity building activities in all states/UTs, including West Bengal, through the Training for All (TFA) scheme.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

2298775.title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ZERO LITIGATION PENSION ECOSYSTEM
2298775.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2298775.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ZERO LITIGATION PENSION ECOSYSTEM
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare is the nodal Department for formulation of policies relating to pension and other retirement benefits of Central Government Civil employees. The 2nd National Workshop on Pension Litigation was convened in pursuance of Government's directives on effective and efficient management of litigation with focus on enhancing coordination and strengthening the capacity/skills of the Nodal officers and panel lawyers of all the Ministries/Departments handling Pension related litigation and its monitoring. It had deliberations and presentations from speakers on the best practices, systemic reforms and grievance redressals to minimize pension litigation towards welfare of pensioners and good governance. The Compendium of case laws and flyer, launched in the Workshop, outlined the best practices in handling pension litigation and recent judicial pronouncements in recurring pension litigation matters providing a comprehensive overview of the concerned pension related policies.

The compendium and flyer underscored the importance of a coordinated approach to managing pension litigation. Pension litigation is not centrally handled by any Department, it is handled on behalf of the Central Government separately by all respective Departments. For minimising litigation, Special Campaign 3 was also launched, wherein focus is on the redressal of the long pending grievances/claims and the issues. This campaign along with other initiatives viz. Pension Adalats and Inter-Ministerial Review Meetings on long pending grievances is an attempt to resolve the grievances, thereby obviating the need to approach courts of law with the resultant effect of reduction in litigation. Further, the Department, based on the clarification and advices sought by various Ministries and Departments, issues Office Memoranda to clarify the rule position to bring ease in the life of the pensioners including super-senior pensioners. The Department, has issued the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972 revised it further by CCS(Pension) Rules, 2021. To ease eligibility conditions of family pensioners, Rule 50 of the said Rules (erstwhile Rule 54 of Rules of 1972) has been provided for various categories of family pensioners including divorced and disabled daughters.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

2298773.title: Empowering Youth, Transforming India
2298773.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Empowering Youth, Transforming India
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:18PM by PIB Delhi

Amrit Peedhi for Viksit Bharat@2047

India is home to one of the world’s largest youth populations, with nearly 65 percent of its citizens below the age of 35. Over the years, the Government has expanded investment across education, skilling, employment, entrepreneurship, sports, health, and civic participation to convert this demographic advantage into a development dividend. Together, these efforts are enabling the Amrit Peedhi to shape Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

MY Bharat: A Platform for Youth-Led Development

At the centre of this vision is Mera Yuva Bharat, launched in October 2023 for youth aged 15–29. The technology-enabled platform brings volunteering, experiential learning, leadership, skilling, career support and civic participation into a single nationwide ecosystem.

  • Growing national platform – More than 2.22 crore youth have registered on the platform for volunteering, experiential learning, leadership, skilling, and career opportunities, as of July 2026.
  • Volunteering at scale – Over 1.52 lakh volunteering opportunities enable young people to participate in community service, environmental action, cultural initiatives and public programmes.
  • Learning through experience – More than 24,900 experiential learning programmes have connected youth with governance, healthcare, media, technology and public service.

Digital Engagement and Civic Participation

  • Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2026 – More than 50 lakh youth participated through a nationwide quiz. The dialogue also involved 78 diaspora youth from 21 countries and identified 6,000 young leaders for a district-wise repository.
  • National Service Scheme (NSS) – Volunteer enrolment increased from 34.09 lakh in 2014–15 to 38.90 lakh in 2025–26.

Education: Access, Quality and Future-Readiness

The education ecosystem has expanded while becoming more flexible, digital and innovation-driven. National Education Policy 2020 places the learner at the centre and links schooling, higher education, skills and employability.

  • One of the world’s largest school systems – India has 14.67 lakh schools serving 24.72 crore students, supported by more than 1.02 crore teachers.
  • Improved retention – The secondary-school dropout rate declined from 14.54 % in 2013–14 to 7 in 2025–26.
  • Digital classrooms – Over 1.49 lakh schools were covered under ICT and digital initiatives by 2025–26, with more than 1.76 lakh smart classrooms and 1.79 lakh ICT laboratories sanctioned (as of March 2026).
  • Atal Tinkering Labs – More than 10,000 labs have engaged over 1.1 crore student innovators and supported more than 16 lakh projects.

Higher Education and Innovation

  • Rising enrolment – Higher-education enrolment increased from 3.4 crore in 2014–15 to 4.5 crore in 2023–24; Female enrolment increased 42.2% since 2014-2015 to 2.2 crores in 2023-24.
  • Institutional growth
     


 

  • Incubation and research – 85 Atal Incubation Centres have created 32,000+ jobs and supported over 2,900 startups.

Flexible Learning and Digital Access

  • National Credit Framework – More than 700 universities and over 7,500 affiliated colleges have adopted the National Credit Framework (NCrF).
  • Academic Bank of Credits – 3,123 institutions have been onboarded and more than 35.27 crore APAAR IDs issued, enabling learners to store, transfer, and redeem credits. (as on 12th August 2026).
  • SWAYAM – As on 12th August 2026, the platform offers more than 20,370 courses and has recorded 6.5 crore+ enrolments.
  • DIKSHA – Across India, 342 courses have recorded 19.06 crore enrolments, 15.02 crore completions, and the issuance of 13 crore certificates (as on 12th August 2026).

Skilling and Employability

The Government has empowered over 6 crore people through its skilling initiatives. Skill India Mission has shifted training from basic certification towards a demand-led model connected with industry, apprenticeships, digital platforms, and emerging technologies.

  • Lower unemployment – The unemployment rate declined from 7.71 per cent in 2014 to 4.2 per cent in 2025.
  • Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) – More than 1.64 crore youth have been trained across four phases since 2015. PMKVY includes industry-linked training in AI, robotics, drones, electronics, green energy, and other future-facing sectors, with on-the-job exposure.
  • Jan Shikshan Sansthan – 36.48 lakh people were trained till March 2026.
  • National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) – More than 54.41 lakh apprentices were engaged till March 2026.
  • Startup India – The number of startups grew from about 350 before 2014 to more than 2.47 lakh by August 2026, making India the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem.
  • Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme - As of 12th August, 2026, the PM Internship Scheme has provided 1,64,902 internship opportunities across 31 sectors.
  • PM-SETU – Launched in October 2025 with an estimated outlay of ₹60,000 crore to upgrade 1,000 government ITIs through 200 hubs and 800 spokes, with industry participation and labor-market-led courses.
  • Between 2014 and 2025, ITIs increased from 9,977 to 14,688; enrolment from 9.5 lakh to 14.7 lakh; National Skill Training Institutes from 25 to 33; and Institutes for Training of
  • Trainers from 11 to 120.

Sports and Fitness

India has built a structured sports pathway that begins with local talent identification and extends to high-performance support. Sport is increasingly seen as a viable career, backed by coaching, infrastructure, scientific training and competition exposure.

  • Khelo India infrastructure – Under the scheme, 349 infrastructure projects worth ₹3,176 crore have been approved, alongside the establishment of 1,067 Khelo India Centres and 267 academies. The scheme also supports 2,745 athletes.
  • Khelo India Games – Since 2018, more than 63,000 athletes have participated in the Youth, University, Winter, Para, Beach, Water Sports and Tribal Games.
  • Support for elite athletes – The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) supports 51 Core, 52 Para Core and 130 Development athletes. Core and Development athletes receive monthly stipends of ₹50,000 and ₹25,000, respectively.
  • Expanded investment – The revamped Khelo India Scheme and enhanced support for National Sports Federations have a combined outlay of ₹36,441 crore for the period 2026–27 to 2030–31.

Health and Well-being

Youth empowerment depends on physical, mental, and preventive healthcare. Government programmes have expanded adolescent-friendly services, mental-health counselling, substance-abuse awareness, and access to comprehensive primary care.

  • Adolescent health – Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics (AFHCs) increased from 6,619 in 2014–15 to 7,203 in 2021–22. Adolescents receiving clinical and counselling services rose from 39 lakh to 82 lakh in the same period; 97.67 lakh youth registered in the clinic in 2024–25 up to November 2024.
  • Mental health – Tele-MANAS has handled over 43.70 lakh calls through 53 cells, supported by 23 mentoring institutes and five Regional Coordinating Centres (as on 12th August 2026).
  • Substance-abuse prevention – As on 12th August, 2026, Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has reached over 30.05 crore people, including 11.86 crore youth. More than 28.56 lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions, while over 28.29 lakh persons have received treatment and rehabilitation support.

A Decade of Transformation

Twelve years of sustained, multi-sectoral investment have produced a measurable transformation in India’s youth. More young Indians are staying in education, acquiring industry-relevant skills, entering formal employment, creating businesses, participating in community life, and competing at the highest levels of sport.

The shift has been from access to opportunity, from participation to leadership, and from youth as beneficiaries to youth as co-creators. Policy, institutions, and digital platforms have laid a strong foundation; the Amrit Peedhi is carrying it forward towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

2298755.title: Expanding the Development Horizon
2298755.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Expanding the Development Horizon
Ensuring Welfare, Inclusion, and Empowerment for Rural and Tribal Communities
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 12:27PM by PIB Delhi

India’s development story is reaching deeper into rural and tribal communities, transforming access, opportunity, and quality of life. From basic services and resilient infrastructure to livelihoods, skills, education, and financial security, interventions are expanding the foundations of inclusive growth. Focused efforts for women, tribal communities, and vulnerable groups are further strengthening pathways to dignity and empowerment. These initiatives are reshaping rural India through wider opportunity, stronger communities, and more equitable development.

From Welfare Delivery to Decentralised Partnerships

  • Direct fiscal transfers to gram panchayats have been increased. It has been increased from ₹2.36 lakh crore under the 15th Finance Commission (2021–26) to ₹4.35 lakh crore under the 16th Finance Commission (2026–31).
  • The Union Budget for rural development has been increased from ₹87,765 crore (2016–17) to ₹2.73 lakh crore (2026–27).
  • The Union Budget for tribal affairs has been increased from ₹4,826 crore (2016–17) to ₹15,421.97 crore (2026–27).

Foundations of Dignity: Universal Access to Basic Needs

Jal Jeevan Mission

  • Household tap water coverage increased from 3.23 crore (August 2019) to over 15.91 crore (August 12, 2026).
  • As of August 12, 2026, 2.89 lakh villages have reported 100% tap water coverage under Har Ghar Jal campaign.

Swachh Bharat Abhiyan - Grameen

  • Over 12.19 crore individual household toilets have been constructed, as of August 12, 2026.
  • India was declared Open Defecation Free in 2019.
  • Over 1,288 GOBARdhan biogas plants are operational, as of August 11, 2026, compared to 14 plants in FY 2018-19.

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana

  • As of August 12, 2026, over 10.57 crore free LPG connections have been provided to women from below-poverty-line households.
  • The total number of LPG connections in India has increased from 14.52 crore in 2014 to 33.39 crore in 2026.

Universal Village Electrification

  • 100% willing household electrification (pan-India level) was achieved by March 2019 under PM Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA).
  • Under the Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana, 100% village electrification was achieved by 2025.

Ayushman Bharat

  • More than 45.51 crore Ayushman Cards have been issued as of August 12, 2026.
  • 96.43 crore ABHA accounts have been created as of August 12, 2026.
  • Over 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are currently functional (as of August 12, 2026).

Food Security for All

  • PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana provides free foodgrains to over 81.35 crore beneficiaries.
  • 99.8% Fair Price Shops under the PDS are automated for Aadhaar-based distribution, as of July 29, 2026.
  • Ration cards are 100% digitised across all States/UTs as of July 29, 2026.
  • As of July 29, 2026, over 221 crore portability transactions have been recorded under One Nation One Ration Card.

Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (Sarva Shiksha Abhiyaan)

  • Between 2018-19 to 2025-26, 4,073 schools have been upgraded and 1.49 lakh ICT and digital initiatives implemented. Further, 25,000 schools are covered under skill education.
  • 97.3% of the schools are equipped with functional female sanitation facilities.
  • Female drop-out rate at primary school level decreased from 4.6% (2013-14) to 0.1% (2025-26). At secondary school level, it reduced from 14.5% (2013-14) to 8% (2025-26).

Reservation for Economically Weaker Section and Improved Enrolment Levels

  • 10% EWS reservation provided for candidates outside existing SC, ST, and OBC reservation categories in 2019. This decision benefits the economically disadvantaged individuals from the general category.
  • In 2025-26, Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) was recorded 89.4 at primary level and 81.5 at secondary level. GER at higher secondary level increased to 61.7 in 2025-26 as compared to 46.4 in 2014-15.

Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

  • Girls’ Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) for girls at the secondary level (Classes 9–10) rose from 75.5% in 2014–15 to 83.4% in 2025–26.

Kasturba Balika Vidyalayas and PM eVidya

  • The number of sanctioned schools increased from 3,609 (2014–15) to 5,639 (2024-25). Operational KGBVs stand at 5,133, as of 2024–25.
  • Enrolment increased from 3.52 lakh (2014–15) to 7.11 lakh (2024).
  • The SWAYAM portal (India’s indigenous MOOC platform) has over 6.5 crore enrolments (as of August 12, 2026).
  • As of August 12, 2026, DIKSHA has 2.35 crore registered users.

Building the Backbone: Infrastructure and Connectivity

 

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Grameen

  • Under PMAY-G, over 3.91 crore houses have been sanctioned, and 3.13 crore houses have been completed (as of August 12, 2026).

Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana

  • As of June 2026, 99.6% of eligible habitations have been connected with all-weather roads.
  • Completed length of roads increased from 3.86 lakh km (May 2000 – May 2014) to 4.13 lakh km (May 2014 – August 12, 2026).
  • Completed number of bridges rose from 484 to 10,404 during May 2014 – August 12, 2026.

Digitalization of Gram Panchayats

  • Under BharatNet, 2.19 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) are connected as of May 2026.
  • Through eGramSwaraj, over ₹3 lakh crore in payments have been processed, as of June 2026.
  • Over 1.28 lakh GPs are using SabhaSaar for creating meeting summaries, as of June 2026.

Pathways to Prosperity: Livelihoods, Skills, and Financial Security

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)

  • As of August 12, 2026, 10.19 crore households have been mobilised into 94.46 lakh SHGs.
  • As of July 29, 2026, 3.46 crore Lakhpati Didis have been created.

Role of Community Resource Persons in Ensuring Last-Mile Delivery of Schemes

  • Over 9 lakh CRPs are currently active, serving thematic areas like agriculture, banking, insurance and nutrition.
  • This includes more than 50,548 Bank Sakhis, 1.91 lakh Krishi Sakhis, 2,012 Matsya Sakhis, and 1.70 lakh Pashu Sakhis.

Introduction of Self-Help Entrepreneur Mart (SHE-Mart)

  • Announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, aiming to benefit 1 crore women.
  • Aims to create community-owned retail spaces for women under the SHG ecosystem.

Deendayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana

  • Candidates trained increased from 43,038 in 2014–15 to 18.45 lakh till August 11, 2026.
  • Candidates placed rose from 21,446 in 2014–15 to 12.35 lakh till August 11, 2026.

Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana

  • Over 1.64 crore youth have received skill training since inception till June 2026.

Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)

  • Total persondays generated between FY 2006-07 to FY 2013-14 were 1,660 crore, whereas, between FY 2014-15 to FY 2024-25, it rose to 3,029 crore.
  • Women’s participation increased from 48% (FY 2013–14) to 58.19% (FY 2024–25).

e-Shram Portal

  • Registrations increased from 14.40 crore (Dec 2021) to 31.87 crore (August 12, 2026).

PM Vishwakarma Yojana

  • As of August 12, 2026, over 30 lakh traditional artisans have been registered.
  • As of August 12, 2026, 24.32 lakh artisans have received skill training and 17.70 lakh have received toolkits.

PM SVANidhi

  • Number of beneficiaries has increased from 26.37 lakh (Nov 2021) to 78.17 lakh (August 12, 2026).
  • As of August 12, 2026, loans amounting to ₹18,971.18 crore have been disbursed. 46% of the beneficiaries are women.

PM MUDRA Yojana

  • Total number of loans sanctioned have increased from 3.49 crore (2016) to over 59.14 crore (July 2026).

PM Jan Dhan Yojana

  • Number of beneficiaries have increased from 17.9 crore (Aug 2015) to 58.90 crore (August 12, 2026).

Expanding Social Security Coverage

  • Under National Pension System, beneficiaries increased from 1.05 crore (2016–17) to 2.17 crore (2025–26).
  • Under Atal Pension Yojana, beneficiaries increased from 48.80 lakh (2016–17) to 9.29 crore (June 2026).
  • 27.90 crore people covered by Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana up to July 2026.
  • 58.78 crore people covered under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana up to July 1, 2026.
  • More than 54 lakh unorganised sector workers have been registered under Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan scheme as of July 2026.

Accelerating Tribal Development through Integrated Interventions

Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN)

  • As of August 5, 2026, 540 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVK) have been sanctioned, benefiting 46,042 persons from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.

 

Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PM-JVM)

  • 4,172 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras sanctioned, benefitting 12.48 lakh tribals under this scheme, as of August 2026.

Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA)

It combines the efforts of 17 ministries and focuses on filling long-standing gaps in tribal-majority villages and PVTG habitations. Under PM JUGA, the emphasis has increasingly moved from isolated interventions to coordinated, mission-mode delivery across sectors and ministries. In last 12 years-

  • 7.60 lakh tribal houses have been completed and 28,303 tribal villages have access to drinking water.
  • 59,812 tribal households and public institutions have been electrified and 657 Anganwadi Centres have been operationalized in tribal areas.
  • 692 hostels have also sanctioned for tribal students.

Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)

  • As of August 12, 2026, over 4.16 lakh Scheduled Caste (SC) houses have been built, over 4.17 lakh SC households are covered under health protection schemes, and more than 3.57 lakh SC households have individual toilets.
  • 17,578 villages have been declared Adarsh Grams as of August 12, 2026.

Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs)

  • Operational schools increased from 129 (2014–15) to 511 (August 12, 2026).
  • As of August 12, 2026, EMRSs have an enrolment of 1.68 lakh students.

PM-YASASVI

  • 20.61 lakh students have received pre-matric scholarship, and 24.53 lakh students have received post-matric scholarship for FY 2024-25.

Scholarships for Scheduled Tribe (ST) Students

  • Between April 2024 and August 12, 2026, Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme has benefitted more than 28.99 lakh tribal students.
  • National Fellowship for ST Students supported 2,961 research scholars in 2025–26. 56% of the beneficiaries were females.

Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)

  • The Top-Class Education for SC Students scheme enabled 8,571 students to study in leading institutions such as IITs, IIMs, NITs and AIIMS in 2025-26.

National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE)

  • 89,915 sewer and septic tank workers and more than 2.81 lakh waste pickers have been validated as of July 2026.

Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-Notified Tribes (SEED)

  • During 2025-26, ₹26.75 crore was disbursed for the educational empowerment of 4,485 De-Notified Tribe (DNT) students.
  • 73,569 Ayushman Bharat cards have been issued to DNT families, under the health component, during 2025-26.

2298712.title: National Biodiversity Authority releases Rs. 15.52 crore ABS Proceeds from Mustard Genetic Resources
2298712.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2298712.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Biodiversity Authority releases Rs. 15.52 crore ABS Proceeds from Mustard Genetic Resources
Amount to be shared among 26 State Biodiversity Boards and 3 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils based on Mustard cultivation area
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 8:44AM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has released Rs. 15.52 crore in Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) proceeds from M/s. Pioneer Overseas Corporation, which developed ten commercial mustard (Brassica juncea) hybrid varieties using India's biological resources. The amount will flow to 26 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and 3 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs), with the ABS share calculated based on the area under mustard cultivation in each State.

M/s. Pioneer Overseas Corporation bred the ten varieties in-house but the parental lines were sourced from the open market and traders. As no single farmer or community could be identified as the source, the NBA constituted an Expert Committee to work out the modalities for ABS disbursal in such cases.

The modalities suggested by the Expert Committee were approved by the Authority. Accordingly, in cases where biological resources are accessed from intermediaries, the ABS is to be shared among the SBBs/UTBCs where the resource is cultivated. The NBA sourced cultivation-area figures from the ICAR–Indian Institute of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (ICAR-IIRMR), Bharatpur, Rajasthan, and used them to calculate each State's share.

Rajasthan, which accounts for nearly 42 per cent of India's mustard cultivation, is receiving the highest benefit, followed by Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. As mustard cultivation is spread across the country, almost every State and Union Territory receives a share proportionately. The top ten ABS receiving States are:

Every SBB and UTBC has to utilise the ABS amount as per Section 32 of the Biological Diversity Act, which includes conservation-linked work; documenting and updating People's Biodiversity Registers; in-situ and ex-situ conservation of biodiversity; restoring degraded ecosystems; strengthening Biodiversity Heritage Sites; building the capacity of Biodiversity Management Committees; improving community livelihoods, among other activities.

The release is part of the NBA's ongoing effort under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, to ensure that when India's genetic resources create commercial value, a fair share flows back to conservation and to the States and communities that sustain that diversity, in line with the Nagoya Protocol and Target 13 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework on fair and equitable benefit sharing.

The NBA has released a total ABS amount of Rs. 182.5 crore so far. It has released Rs. 116.22 crore to beneficiaries across the country in the last 12 months.

About the National Biodiversity Authority

The National Biodiversity Authority is a statutory body established under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, functioning under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. It regulates access to India's biological resources and associated knowledge and implements the Nagoya Protocol's principle of fair and equitable sharing of benefits.

2298703.title: PRESS RELEASE ON 393rd REPORT OF THE DEPARTMENT-RELATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE
2298703.body_html:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
PRESS RELEASE ON 393rd REPORT OF THE DEPARTMENT-RELATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 10:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture headed by Shri Sanjay Kumar Jha, M.P., Rajya Sabha, presented its 393rd Report on “From Manuscript to Mission: Preserving, Mapping and Sustaining India’s Cultural Heritage in the Age of Artificial Intelligence” on Wednesday, the 12th August, 2026.

  1. The Report was adopted by the Committee on 11th August, 2026. The Key Recommendations/Observations made by the Committee in this Report are enclosed.

 

The full Report is available on the website of Rajya Sabha https://sansad.in/rs -→Committees→Department related RS→Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture-→ Report

 

THE THREE HUNDRED NINETY THIRD REPORT OF DEPARTMENT-REL koi ATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE

 

SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Enlarge the digitisation standard into a complete capture standard, settled in consultation with scholars, scientists and custodians and in force before the contracts reach full scale: a multispectral recovery tier for damaged and overwritten folios; surface-relief imaging as the standard for palm leaf; a materials record for significant manuscripts; and a dating protocol anchored at Indian accelerator laboratories with margins stated on the record. (Paragraph 5.1.2)

 

2. Institute, with the national scientific departments, a research and challenge programme to read manuscripts that cannot be opened, beginning with a census of fused and fire-damaged holdings. (Paragraph 5.2.2)

 

3. Build the national reading workforce: the Akshar Mitra citizen platform with two independent checks on every page and permanent contributor credit; the university compact under which unedited manuscripts become dissertation editions recognised as research of the first rank; and published priority lists so that effort chases textual value. (Paragraph 5.3.2)

4. Release every publicly funded page and verified transcription as an open national library of training pages with an annual public benchmark, and employ federated learning so that restricted collections contribute without an image leaving custody. (Paragraph 5.4.2)

 

5. Publish the open index of persons, places and works of the corpus, the time-layered atlas of Indian knowledge built upon it, and the register of scribal hands. (Paragraph 5.5.2)

 

6. Extract the astronomical and weather observations of the corpus, with the national scientific agencies, as open national datasets for Indian science. (Paragraph 5.6.2)

 

7. Constitute the standing programme to reunite the scattered corpus: a common catalogue of dispersed and overseas holdings; exchange of images; virtual rebinding by computer matching of leaves and hands; and the identification of Indian manuscripts held overseas, the acquisition of digital copies of them and steps to bring back originals where return can be secured, with reunified treasures proposed for the Memory of the World register. (Paragraph 5.7.2)

 

8. Build, with the Ministry of Ayush, the concordance connecting manuscript formulations to the national terminologies and the statutory pharmacopoeia. (Paragraph 5.8.2)

 

9. Build the Repository's architecture of trust: the international image interoperability framework as the access standard; community access protocols under which every custodian chooses, item by item, what is shown; and an embedded credential in every machine-produced rendering, with the Ministry advocating its preservation with the major platforms. (Paragraph 5.9.2)

 

10. Serve the living inheritance: oral heritage recorded through Indian-language speech recognition, beginning with the fewest surviving bearers; fonts, keyboards and voices for every encoded script, freely downloadable and offered to the major operating systems; and the technique of the last masters recorded in three dimensions, with personal designation, lifetime grant and successor duties. (Paragraph 5.10.2)

 

11. Put the map to work: the cultural and manuscript layers on the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan and in district planning; knowledge tourism circuits designed from them; and the mapped artisan joined to commerce through the Open Network for Digital Commerce with authenticity credentials linked to the map. (Paragraph 5.11.2)

 

  1. Establish the guardianship framework: the machine-graded register of manuscripts at risk with preservation kits and connected loggers for custodians; district salvage annexes wired into the national alerting infrastructure with cultural first-aid training; and a published preservation architecture of distributed copies and a deep archive on century-lasting media. (Paragraph 5.12.2)

2298681.title: India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU)  sign Terms of Reference (ToR) for negotiations towards a Preferential Trade Agreement
2298681.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU)  sign Terms of Reference (ToR) for negotiations towards a Preferential Trade Agreement
Union Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Balanced and Equitable India–SACU Trade Agreement
India Can Support Affordable Medicines, IT Talent and Global Supply Chain Integration in SACU Region: Shri Goyal
Negotiations to cover eight important chapters, including trade in goods, market access for goods and rules of origin: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 9:36PM by PIB Delhi

India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) today signed the Terms of Reference (ToR) for negotiations towards a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) between India and SACU at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The signing marks an important step towards strengthening trade and economic engagement between India and the SACU Member States.

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal called for a balanced, fair and equitable trade agreement between India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU), emphasising that the partnership can help diversify markets and create opportunities for both sides to prosper. Shri Goyal said India can play an important role in supplying affordable medicines and supporting the development of new talent in the IT sector in the SACU region. Shri Goyal added that India can also help integrate SACU countries into global supply chains in areas where their businesses are competitive and where skills and talent can be developed or are already available.

The Minister stated that India’s engagement with Southern Africa is rooted in a longstanding partnership of equals and extends well beyond trade. He recalled that Southern Africa occupies a special place in India’s national memory, noting that “India’s relationship with Southern Africa did not begin with commerce. It began with conscience.” Recalling Mahatma Gandhi, he also highlighted India’s support for the peoples of Southern Africa in their struggle against apartheid.

Shri Goyal underscored that the negotiations seek to provide preferential market access to an already established commercial relationship, with significant complementarities in engineering goods and machinery, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, textiles, agriculture and agri-processing. He called upon the negotiating teams to proceed with urgency and stressed the importance of translating the agreed Terms of Reference into a concrete process towards early finalisation of the India–SACU PTA. He further noted, “What we sign today does not by itself lower a single tariff or clear a single container. Only a final agreement will do that,” and called for an early conclusion of the PTA.

The signing ceremony was attended by Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada, senior officials from the Government of India and the SACU delegation.

Executive Director, Ministry of International Relations and Trade, Government of the Republic of Namibia, Ms. Ndiitah Nghipondoka-Robiati welcomed the signing of the ToR as an important milestone in formalising SACU–India engagement and providing structure, transparency and predictability to the forthcoming negotiations. Highlighting India’s importance as a strategic partner and a pillar of South–South cooperation, she noted the longstanding relationship between India and Africa through trade, investment, capacity building and development cooperation. She emphasised that SACU attaches real importance to an outcome that is balanced and takes into account the different levels of development among the Parties, particularly the interests and development needs of SACU Member States, including its Least Developed Countries and Small and Vulnerable Economies.

Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, addressing the gathering, said that this is India’s first ToR signing with the African region and noted SACU’s significance as the oldest customs union in the world. He stated that the PTA is envisaged to cover eight important chapters, including trade in goods and market access for goods; rules of origin and origin procedures; customs procedures and trade facilitation; trade remedies, including a bilateral safeguard mechanism; sanitary and phytosanitary measures; technical barriers to trade; dispute settlement; and legal and horizontal provisions.

The signing of the ToR reflects the shared commitment of India and SACU to advance mutually beneficial trade relations and lays the foundation for negotiations towards a balanced, mutually beneficial and development-oriented PTA.

2298663.title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS SHRI KOVIND’S STORY AS AN ENDURING SOURCE OF “INSPIRATION FOR GENERATIONS”
2298663.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS SHRI KOVIND’S STORY AS AN ENDURING SOURCE OF “INSPIRATION FOR GENERATIONS”
PRIME MINISTER RELEASES AUTOBIOGRAPHY OF FORMER PRESIDENT SHRI RAM NATH KOVIND
SHRI KOVIND’S AUTOBIOGRAPHY PRESENTS AN EXTRAORDINARY JOURNEY OF STRUGGLE, RESOLVE, AND ACHIEVEMENT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
SHRI KOVIND UPHELD CONSTITUTIONAL TRADITIONS WITH UNWAVERING COMMITMENT TO SOCIAL HARMONY AND INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
DURING COVID-19 PANDEMIC, SHRI KOVIND INSTILLED COURAGE AND CONFIDENCE AMONG PEOPLE AND MADE RASHTRAPATI BHAVAN MORE ACCESSIBLE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 9:08PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today released the autobiography of former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind, titled ‘Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles’ at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla was present on the occasion and described the release of the book as a matter of great pride and significance.

Speaking at the distinguished gathering, Shri Birla observed that the autobiography of former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind, an embodiment of high constitutional ideals, presents an extraordinary journey of determination, struggle, and achievement. Recalling the challenges of Shri Kovind’s early life, including the difficulties he faced in pursuing his education, he said that his journey from a humble and economically disadvantaged background to the highest constitutional office of the country reflects his extraordinary resolve and serves as an enduring source of inspiration for generations to come.

The Lok Sabha Speaker noted that Shri Kovind’s unwavering commitment to constitutional values enabled him to leave an indelible mark as an advocate. His tenure as a Member of Parliament, he said, was marked by dedication to the welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, social justice, and probity in public life.

Referring to Shri Kovind’s tenure as Governor, Shri Birla mentioned that he provided a new direction to transparency, quality, and technological innovation in higher education. As President of India, he upheld the constitutional traditions of Indian democracy and demonstrated an unwavering commitment to social harmony and inclusive development. Further, through his visits to several countries, he also contributed to strengthening India’s international diplomatic relations, he added.

Shri Birla also mentioned that during the challenging period of the COVID-19 pandemic, Shri Kovind instilled courage, unity, and confidence among the people of the country and made the Rashtrapati Bhavan more accessible to the public. He described this as one of Shri Kovind’s significant achievements.

The Lok Sabha Speaker added that even after demitting the office of President, Shri Kovind continues to contribute to the nation, the Constitution, and society through his vast experience, reflections on public life, and commitment to social justice. Shri Birla expressed confidence that ‘Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles’ would bring before readers important episodes from Shri Kovind’s life and inspire them to play a purposive role in public life. He concluded by extending his warm congratulations and best wishes to Shri Ram Nath Kovind on the publication of the book.

2298661.title: Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) and NITI Aayog Sign Statement of Intent to Advance Multilingual AI for Inclusive Governance
2298661.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) and NITI Aayog Sign Statement of Intent to Advance Multilingual AI for Inclusive Governance
Partnership to Enable Voice-First, Multilingual AI for Citizen-Centric Governance and Public Service Delivery
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, and NITI Aayog, Government of India, have signed a Statement of Intent (SoI) to collaborate on advancing multilingual, voice-first AI solutions for inclusive governance and citizen-centric public service delivery through the BHASHINI for Seva/Sanchalan initiative.

The SoI was signed by Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, and Shri Shoyabahmed Kalal, Director, NITI Aayog.

The collaboration aims to leverage BHASHINI's multilingual AI ecosystem to enable more inclusive and accessible governance by integrating AI-powered language technologies across NITI Aayog's digital platforms and services. The partnership will facilitate access to government information and services in citizens' preferred Indian languages, strengthen communication between government and citizens, and promote multilingual operations across public service delivery.

Under the SoI, both organisations will collaborate across BHASHINI Udyat, BHASHINI Mitra, BHASHINI AppMitra, BHASHINI Sahayogi and BHASHINI Pravakta. The partnership will facilitate multilingual access to NITI Aayog services through BHASHINI's language translation APIs and reference applications, support the development and continuous improvement of translation models, and enable the integration of language technologies into digital platforms, document management systems and communication workflows.

The collaboration will also support the development of reference applications and voice bots for specific NITI Aayog sectors and strengthen language technology for specialised terminology and sector-specific requirements. Through BHASHINI Sahayogi, the partnership will leverage BhashaDaan for the collection, curation and dissemination of linguistic data, with NITI Aayog officials and citizens encouraged to contribute text, audio and video samples.

Through BHASHINI Pravakta, the two organisations will work towards expanding awareness and adoption of BHASHINI's services, tools and resources across districts, supported by training, technical assistance and resources to ensure that multilingual digital solutions remain accessible to users with varying levels of digital literacy.

The collaboration also builds on NITI TARA (Toolkit for Analysis, Review & Action), which is transforming data into action at the grassroots. With 200+ capacity-building sessions conducted across the country, NITI TARA has empowered over 4,000 officials from districts and blocks to leverage data-driven insights for evidence-based decision-making. Through interactive multi-sectoral dashboards, intuitive visualisations and collaborative planning tools, the platform is simplifying reviews, strengthening inter-departmental coordination and enabling more effective governance.

An important component of this ecosystem is SMRITI (System for Meeting Recording, Information & Transcription Interface), developed in collaboration with BHASHINI. By automating meeting minutes and enabling multilingual translation, SMRITI is enhancing operational efficiency while making governance more inclusive at the last mile.

The collaboration is expected to contribute to bridging language barriers, enabling bidirectional communication between government and the public, and promoting multilingual operations for more inclusive public service delivery.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. Today, BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 24 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, making Digital Public Infrastructure more accessible through Language AI.

2298635.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah launches the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app via video conferencing; the app was developed to interconnect libraries in the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency of Gujarat
2298635.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah launches the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app via video conferencing; the app was developed to interconnect libraries in the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency of Gujarat
‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ is a new initiative; its objective is to establish a library in every village to encourage children to read
752 libraries have joined the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app so far
Four libraries containing 2.80 lakh books have been linked with these rural libraries
The process of opening 63 libraries—each stocked with five to six thousand books—has begun across all villages in the Gandhinagar, Kalol, and Sanand assembly constituencies
Home Minister has personally prepared a list of books for libraries—books that will spark an interest in reading among children and inspire them to dive into the vast ocean of knowledge
Vans provided through the MPLADs will visit villages every fortnight to collect previously distributed books and deliver books registered on the app to village libraries
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today launched the 'Gramin Gyan Setu' app developed to integrate the libraries of Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency of Gujarat through video conferencing.

Addressing the event virtually, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah noted that today marks the birth anniversary of S.R. Ranganathan. He stated that the entire nation is celebrating the birth anniversary of Padma Shri Ranganathan as National Library Day, and that a new idea and concept—‘Gramin Gyan Setu’—has been launched in his Lok Sabha constituency. Shri Shah stated that the objective is to establish a library in every village—located centrally and near the school—to encourage children to engage with reading and learning. He noted that approximately 63 libraries have already been set up. Initiatives have been launched to open small libraries, each housing five to six thousand books, across all villages in the Gandhinagar, Kalol, and Sanand assembly constituencies. Union Home Minister mentioned that he personally curated a list of books for these multi-purpose, multi-dimensional libraries—books designed to spark an interest in reading among children and gradually inspire them to immerse themselves in the vast ocean of knowledge. Additionally, the libraries will stock books beneficial for the career development of adolescents and youth, as well as resources for state and national-level competitive examinations. Arrangements have also been made to ensure the availability of books covering the history of Gujarat, the history of the nation, the story of the freedom struggle, and the Revolution of 1857 right within the village.

Shri Amit Shah stated that cultivating a reading habit in children is not possible without encouragement from parents; however, for children who are motivated to study, four libraries—collectively housing 2.80 lakh books that will benefit them in the future—have been linked to these rural libraries. Union Home Minister mentioned that he has facilitated this service by arranging vans using his MP Local Area Development (MPLAD) funds. These vans will visit the villages every fortnight to collect previously issued books and deliver books registered on the app to the village libraries. He noted that children who are accustomed to visiting libraries containing 6,000 to 7,000 books will now have access to a collection of 2.80 lakh books.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated that while he had originally proposed the idea, Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel and the Gujarat government have integrated it with a new scientific approach. He noted that 752 libraries are now connected to the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app. He emphasized that without study, it is impossible to gain even basic knowledge, let alone achieve mastery in any subject. He added that as individuals transition from childhood to adolescence, then to youth, and finally to adulthood, guidance from competent librarians regarding studies and their various dimensions can enable libraries to play a pivotal role in shaping citizens who are valuable to the nation.

Shri Amit Shah stated that the Mahatma Gandhi Library in Mansa has been linked to this library-related scheme. He mentioned that at the Mahatma Gandhi Library, he acquired basic knowledge across various subjects and gained in-depth understanding of some over a period of 16 years. After moving from Mansa to Ahmedabad, he became associated with the Gujarat Vidyapith library. He noted that Kakasaheb Kalelkar had created the Gujarat Vidyapith library as a means for many young people—like himself—to dive into the ocean of knowledge. The urge to gather information on every subject evolved into a habit, which subsequently transformed into a practice of study. He remarked that it was this practice of study that enabled him to contribute to a specific field, and the library played a pivotal role in this process.

Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated that these libraries and books have now been made available to the youth through the ‘hub-and-spoke’ model. While such facilities did not exist in his time, this program is now scientifically accessible to the current generation. He expressed his aim to have various institutions—such as Sastu Sahitya Mandal, Gita Press, the Bhupen Hazarika Institute, and the Thiruvalluvar Institute—connect online with libraries in Gujarat’s Gandhinagar district and at the state level. He expressed confidence that this facility would become available to students and readers through the use of technology.

Shri Amit Shah urged housewives across the country and the state to make productive use of their spare time by acquiring knowledge on various subjects and encouraging their children to study.

President Droupadi Murmu asks Commission to envision measures to strengthen,  streamline existing institutional mechanisms, ensuring more effective implementation of safeguards and welfare measures for Scheduled Castes
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 8:28PM by PIB Delhi

The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) submitted its Annual Report for 2024–25 to Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhawan, in National Capital today.

This is in line with the Constitutional mandate under Article 338 of the Constitution of India on the working of the Constitutional Safeguards for the Scheduled Castes which include recommendations for measures to be taken by the Union and the State Governments for the effective implementation as well as for the protection, welfare, and socio-economic development of Scheduled Castes.

The annual report was presented by a high level delegation led by Chairman, NCSC, Shri Kishor Makwana alongwith Members, NCSC, Shri Love Kush Kumar, Shri Vaddepalli Ramchander and Dr. Partha Biswas and the Secretary, NCSC, Shri Gudey Srinivas.

The Hon’ble President directed the Commission to envision measures aimed at strengthening and streamlining the existing mechanisms for the effective implementation of Constitutional safeguards and welfare measures for the Scheduled Castes, with a view to ensuring the smooth and effective functioning of the institutional mechanisms for their welfare and socio-economic development.

The Report presents a comprehensive review of the functioning of the Constitutional provisions for Scheduled Castes. It outlines key findings from extensive reviews, spot visits and consultations with Central and State Governments regarding the implementation of welfare schemes and socio-economic development programmes for Scheduled Castes.

2298602.title: Union Health Minister Shri Nadda interacts with MPs from Jharkhand and Odisha to strengthen efforts towards TB Mukt Bharat
2298602.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2298602.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister Shri Nadda interacts with MPs from Jharkhand and Odisha to strengthen efforts towards TB Mukt Bharat
MPs commit to intensify awareness, strengthen oversight and mobilise communities for TB elimination
Shri Nadda calls for sustained parliamentary engagement and district-level oversight to accelerate TB elimination
Parliamentarians from Jharkhand and Odisha unite to strengthen last-mile TB services
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 8:15PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today interacted with Members of Parliament from Jharkhand and Odisha on the sidelines of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, as part of the Government’s continued engagement with parliamentarians to accelerate efforts towards a TB Mukt Bharat. Smt. Anupriya Patel, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare & Chemicals and Fertilizers, and Shri Sanjay Seth, Union Minister of State for Defence, also participated in the interaction.

The interaction, held under the theme “Parliamentarians Championing a TB Mukt Bharat”, brought together Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs from both States across party lines, reflecting a shared commitment to strengthening the fight against tuberculosis through political leadership, community participation and last-mile delivery of services.

The interaction reviewed progress under the recently concluded 100-Day TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, which was implemented in two phases to accelerate TB elimination efforts. The second phase, launched on March 24, 2026, covered nearly 1.58 lakh high-risk villages and urban wards across the country and concluded in July 2026.

During the campaign, over 2.2 crore vulnerable individuals were screened, more than 7 lakh new TB cases were detected, and 1.97 lakh asymptomatic TB cases were identified—cases that may otherwise have remained undetected. The intensified case-finding approach has demonstrated the importance of proactive screening, particularly among vulnerable and high-risk populations.

India has made significant progress in TB elimination, recording a 21% decline in TB incidence between 2015 and 2024, nearly twice the global pace, along with a 92% treatment success rate, according to the WHO Global TB Report 2025. The intensified focus on early detection, treatment and patient support is central to sustaining this momentum.

Jharkhand and Odisha remain important focus States given the presence of several TB risk factors, including mining and industrial belts, occupational dust exposure, migrant and tribal populations, malnutrition, urban slums, comorbidities, tobacco and alcohol consumption, and informal and labour settlements.

During the 100-Day campaign, Jharkhand notified 16,754 TB patients, including 4,574 asymptomatic cases, while Odisha notified 15,268 patients, including 3,514 asymptomatic cases.

The States adopted targeted strategies to take screening and care closer to vulnerable populations, including through Ayushman Arogya Shivirs in urban slums, construction sites, migrant clusters and mining areas.

The technological expansion of India’s TB programme has further strengthened these efforts. Molecular testing capacity has expanded from a few hundred machines a decade ago to more than 9,000 machines, while nearly 3,000 AI-enabled handheld X-ray units are now supporting active case finding in the field.

Shri Nadda emphasised the importance of sustained political and administrative engagement in achieving the goal of a TB Mukt Bharat. He highlighted innovative case-finding strategies, early diagnosis, patient-centric care and community participation as critical pillars of India’s accelerated TB elimination strategy.

He called upon parliamentarians to play an active role in their constituencies by engaging with District Collectors and health facilities, reviewing the availability and quality of TB services, and supporting efforts for early diagnosis and treatment. He also stressed the need for continued public engagement and social mobilisation to ensure that TB elimination becomes a sustained Jan Andolan.

The participating MPs from Jharkhand and Odisha reaffirmed their commitment to intensifying awareness and stigma-reduction campaigns, promoting Ni-kshay Shivirs for early detection, particularly among vulnerable populations, and strengthening supportive supervision of TB services at district and block levels.

The parliamentarians also committed to mobilising communities and organisations to provide nutritional, psychosocial and livelihood support to people affected by TB, thereby strengthening the patient-centric approach to TB care.

The interaction is part of a series of consultations being held by the Union Health Minister with Members of Parliament from different States to strengthen collective ownership and a whole-of-government approach towards achieving a TB Mukt Bharat.

Shri Nadda expressed confidence that sustained engagement by parliamentarians, State and district administrations, healthcare workers and communities will further accelerate progress towards TB elimination, with the conclusion of the 100-Day campaign serving as a platform for deeper and continued action at the grassroots level.

Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava highlighted the focused efforts being undertaken in Jharkhand and Odisha to address TB among vulnerable and priority populations, including communities in mining and industrial areas, migrant and tribal populations, urban settlements, and groups requiring additional support due to factors such as malnutrition and comorbidities. She emphasised the importance of targeted screening, early detection and accessible patient-centric care to further strengthen TB elimination efforts in both States. She shared that Jharkhand notified 16,754 TB patients during the 100-Day campaign, including 4,574 asymptomatic cases, while Odisha notified 15,268 patients, including 3,514 asymptomatic cases. She emphasised the need for continued intensified screening and targeted interventions among vulnerable populations to sustain the momentum towards TB elimination.

Additional Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik highlighted the technological foundation underpinning India’s intensified TB case-finding efforts. She noted that India has expanded molecular testing capacity from a few hundred machines a decade ago to more than 9,000 machines, supported by nearly 3,000 AI-enabled handheld X-ray units deployed in the field.

She also presented an overview of Jharkhand and Odisha’s performance across key indicators, including TB notifications, treatment success, preventive therapy coverage and progress against national TB elimination benchmarks.

Smt. Patnaik highlighted that during the 100-Day campaign, both States adopted targeted strategies to take screening and care closer to vulnerable populations, including through Ayushman Arogya Shivirs in urban slums, construction sites, migrant clusters and mining areas. These approaches helped strengthen active case finding and bring TB services closer to communities that may otherwise face barriers in accessing diagnosis and treatment.

The collective commitment of the parliamentarians, State and district administrations, healthcare workers and communities is expected to further strengthen the national resolve towards achieving a TB Mukt Bharat.

2298552.title: Three Sanchar Mitras Selected as ITU Generation Connect Youth Envoys for the period 2026–2030
2298552.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Three Sanchar Mitras Selected as ITU Generation Connect Youth Envoys for the period 2026–2030
Recognition highlights growing role of Indian youth in shaping the global digital future
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi

With an objective of creating opportunities for India’s youth to learn, participate, lead and contribute to the evolving digital future at the international level, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India, has facilitated the selection of three Sanchar Mitras (youth volunteers) from India as Generation Connect Youth Envoys (GCYE) of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). This comes as the global community celebrates International Youth Day 2026 under the theme “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations”. The Generation Connect community marked the occasion through the virtual “Passing the Torch: Connecting Generations of Digital Leaders” event today , bringing together the outgoing and incoming cohorts of Generation Connect Youth Envoys.

Ankit Kumar Pal from Delhi, Manish Kumar Mandal from Bengaluru and Susmita Sain from Guwahati have been selected as part of the third cohort of ITU Generation Connect Youth Envoys for the period 2026–2030 in recognition of their contribution under the Sanchar Mitra scheme of DoT. Their selection marks an important recognition of the growing role of Indian youth in shaping the global digital future.

The Generation Connect Youth Envoys programme provides young people with opportunities to contribute to national, regional and global discussions and initiatives related to Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs), digital transformation and inclusive digital development.

The initiative aligns closely with the objectives of the Sanchar Mitra Scheme, which seeks to engage young people in telecom and digital initiatives and provide them exposure to national and international platforms. The scheme also envisages opportunities for selected Sanchar Mitras to participate in global telecom platforms such as the ITU.

Following ITU’s invitation for nominations to the third cohort of Generation Connect Youth Envoys, the Department of Telecommunications initiated a process to identify suitable candidates from among Sanchar Mitras. The process sought candidates with demonstrated engagement in areas including youth-led initiatives, digital inclusion, ICT education and skills, research and technical activities, entrepreneurship and innovation, and community-level ICT initiatives.

The recognition also reflects India’s commitment to empowering young people as active contributors to the country’s digital transformation journey and strengthening youth participation in global conversations on technology, connectivity and inclusive digital development.

Through initiatives such as Sanchar Mitra and its engagement with global platforms including the ITU Generation Connect programme, the Department of Telecommunications continues to create opportunities for India’s youth to learn, participate, lead and contribute to the evolving digital future.

About Sanchar Mitra

The Sanchar Mitra Scheme envisions to engage the Yuva Shakti- India’s youth, as catalysts for digital empowerment and societal outreach. The students nominated as Sanchar Mitra actively conduct awareness drives in communities, educational institutions, public spaces, etc., focusing on key telecom-related issues, like citizen-centric telecom services, prevention of telecom frauds and mobile security - promoting digital safety, and foster responsible telecom usage.

This scheme is open to students from those technical institutes that have active telecom, electronics, computers, cybersecurity or similar programs and have agreed to participate in the scheme.

The scheme has been implemented across all states/ UTs through the LSA field offices of DoT. More than 200 institutions are currently participating in it.

2298542.title: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) Launches e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services
2298542.body_html:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) Launches e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi

The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) today launched its e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services. Hon’ble President, NCLT, Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal, inaugurated the services through video conferencing, marking another step towards making the Tribunal’s Registry more accessible and technology-enabled.

Speaking on the occasion, Justice Grewal said that the two services are intended to provide advocates, litigants and other stakeholders with convenient and faster access to judicial records and certified copies. The services form part of the Tribunal’s broader digital transformation, including the revamped NCLT website and the ongoing e-Courts 2.0 initiative.

The Hon’ble NCLT President also highlighted the measures undertaken to improve case management and reduce pendency. The NCLT has adopted a data-driven mechanism to monitor pendency across Benches. Based on the data so collated, workload was reviewed and redistributed, Special Benches were constituted wherever required, and efforts were made to maximise the available Court time.

These measures contributed to the approval of 78 resolution plans during April–June 2026, the highest first-quarter performance since the enactment of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, involving approximately ₹5,517.66 crore.

The NCLT has also issued detailed guidelines on registration and listing of cases, in consultation with the Bar, to ensure optimum utilisation of limited judicial resources.

Justice Grewal emphasised that while the Tribunal continues to face infrastructural and manpower constraints, sustained efforts are being made to reduce avoidable delays and improve efficiency.

The launch of the two services is part of the NCLT’s continuing endeavour to provide a more transparent, efficient and stakeholder-oriented system of justice delivery.

2298538.title: Smt Archana Varma Takes Charge as Secretary, Department of Water Resources, RD & GR, Ministry of Jal Shakti
2298538.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Smt Archana Varma Takes Charge as Secretary, Department of Water Resources, RD & GR, Ministry of Jal Shakti
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi

Smt. Archana Varma assumed charge as Secretary, Department of Water Resources, RD & GR, Ministry of Jal Shakti, on 12 August 2026. She is a 1995-batch IAS officer of the Assam cadre. Upon assuming charge, she was welcomed by Joint Secretary (Admn.), Shri Karan Singh, and other officials of the Department.

Prior to this, Smt. Varma served in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Department of Personnel and Training, and held several senior positions in the Government of India. She also served as Additional Secretary in the Central Vigilance Commission, where she handled matters relating to the Commission’s policies and vigilance issues concerning the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, among others.

In September, 2022, she joined Ministry of Jal Shakti as Mission Director, National Water Mission (NWM) and worked on taking the NWM beyond JSA - CTR.

Smt. Varma began her career as the Sub-Divisional Magistrate of Hamren, in the Sixth Schedule tribal District of Karbi Anglong in Assam, now the West Karbi Anglong District and has held several important positions in the State Government.

Smt. Archana Varma is a graduate in History from Lady Shri Ram College and a postgraduate from Jawaharlal Nehru University.
