2298160.title: IMPLEMENTATION OF RASHTRIYA GRAM SWARAJ ABHIYAN (RGSA) IN WEST BENGAL
2298160.body_html:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
IMPLEMENTATION OF RASHTRIYA GRAM SWARAJ ABHIYAN (RGSA) IN WEST BENGAL
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi

Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject and part of the State list of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/ UTs. The main objective of the scheme is to strengthen the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by imparting training to Elected Representatives (ERs), Panchayat Functionaries and other stakeholders to develop their governance capabilities for leadership roles, enabling the Gram Panchayats and Local bodies to function effectively across all States/UTs including the State of West Bengal.

Apart from different trainings, the Scheme also supports development of Panchayat infrastructure like Gram Panchayat Bhawan, Computer and Co-location (on a limited scale) of Common Service Centers (CSCs) in Gram Panchayat Bhawan to the States/ UTs including in the State of West Bengal.

Under Revamped RGSA, the Central Empowered Committee of RGSA accords approval to the units under various components based on the Annual Action Plan (AAP) submitted by the State/UT. During the last four years (FY 2022-23 to FY 2025-26), an amount of Rs.130.65 crore was released as Central Share to the State of West Bengal under the Scheme. Out of which, Rs.268.26 crore has been utilized by the State. Utilization of funds includes Central Share, State Share and unspent balance from previous years.

A total of 5,17,632 elected representatives of the State of West Bengal were trained on various aspects on rural governance from FY 2022-23 to FY 2025-26. In addition, 199 units for the construction of Panchayat Bhawans and 1,712 units of Computers were approved under the scheme from FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26. The State has reported that 124 Panchayat Bhawan have been constructed and 1,185 units of computers have been procured during FY 2023-24 to 2026-27 (as on 5th August 2026).

The State has also reported that all stakeholders of Panchayati Raj Institutions are invited to participate in various training programmes conducted under the Scheme.

Revamped RGSA is demand-driven in nature. Funds are released to States/UTs based on the Annual Action Plans approved by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC), the pace of expenditure by the State and submission of requisite document for release of funds. The funds are utilized only for the approved components as prioritized by the States/UTs. The Ministry releases the funds under the scheme to States/UTs only. Rs.8.00 crore as Central Share in the 1st Instalment was released to the State of West Bengal in the FY 2026-27 (as on 10th July 2026).

As informed by the State, 199 units of the construction of Gram Panchayat Bhawans have been approved from FY 2023-24 to 2025-26 under the scheme of Revamped RGSA, out of which 124 units have been completed till 5th August 2026 and remaining 75 units are different stages of completion. As per the information submitted in the Annual Action Plan of RGSA in the FY 2025-26 by the State, only 87 Gram Panchayats out of 3,339 do not have own building. Under Revamped RGSA Scheme, component wise fund has not been released to the States/UTs. State/UTs utilized the funds based on the approved components of their AAPs as per the priority.

To promote e-enablement of Panchayats, the Ministry is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP), which has strengthened transparency, efficiency and governance at the grassroots level. As per the information available on Government e Marketplace (GeM) Portal, 267 Panchayats have adopted/ on-boarded on GeM. 1,881 Gram Panchayats have uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plan on eGramSwaraj Portal for the Plan Year 2026-27 in the State of West Bengal as on 06.08.2026. As informed by the State Govt. of West Bengal, a total of 10,111 elected representatives have been trained as on date under the scheme in FY 2026-27.

This information was given by Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on 12th August 2026.

2298159.title: STRENGTHENING DIGITAL PANCHAYAT GOVERNANCE THROUGH EGRAMSWARAJ
2298159.body_html:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
STRENGTHENING DIGITAL PANCHAYAT GOVERNANCE THROUGH EGRAMSWARAJ
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 2:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) with the objective of strengthening transparency, efficiency, and accountability in the functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through digital enablement across all States. The eGramSwaraj application has been integrated with various digital governance platforms to enhance planning, financial management and service delivery in Panchayati Raj Institutions. The major integrations are as follows:

  • Public Financial Management System (PFMS): For online fund management, accounting and end-to-end digital payments to vendors and beneficiaries.
  • Government e-Marketplace (GeM): To facilitate procurement of goods and services by Panchayati Raj Institutions in a transparent and efficient manner.
  • BSNL: To enable panchayat to apply for new internet connection and bill payment of BharatNet connection through eGramSwaraj.
  • BHASHINI: To provide multilingual and AI-enabled language translation and voice-based services for improved accessibility of the platform.
  • India Meteorological Department (IMD): To provide weather-related information for supporting local planning and decision-making by Panchayati Raj Institutions.

These integrations have been made available through the eGramSwaraj platform for all States and expected to benefit all Gram Panchayats across the country using the eGramSwaraj platform.

Further, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj launched SabhaSaar, an AI-enabled voice-to-text meeting summarisation tool, that enables structured capture and summarisation of Gram Sabha proceedings and supports monitoring of key parameters such as frequency and type of Gram Sabha meetings and participation. The platform captures agenda-wise discussions, decisions, and participation details, and the generated minutes are made available to Panchayat functionaries for review, validation and final acceptance. SabhaSaar has been made available to all States/UTs.

During the FY 2025–26, out of a total of 2,58,725 Gram Panchayats and equivalent across the States, 2,55,251 (98.65%) of them have uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) on e-Gram Swaraj and 2,45,839 Gram Panchayats and equivalents (95%) have made payments amounting to ₹57,337 crore through the e-GramSwaraj–PFMS interface. Further a total of 1,35,956 Gram Panchayats and equivalent have used the SabhaSaar tool for automated meeting summarization and over 3,57,020 minutes of the meeting have been processed across States/UTs.

These initiatives are expected to enhance transparency through digital workflows and real-time monitoring, improve accountability by ensuring standardized planning and financial management processes, facilitate evidence-based decision-making through dashboards and reports, reduce manual intervention, and promote ease of governance by providing an integrated digital platform for planning, accounting, monitoring, and implementation of Panchayat activities.

 

This information was given by Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on 12th August 2026.

2298157.title: Reforming India’s Tribunal System
2298157.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Reforming India’s Tribunal System
Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 2:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026 seeks to create a more independent, transparent and professionally administered tribunal system. The Bill provides for setting up of a judiciary-led  National Tribunals Commission that will make selections to the tribunals and exercise oversight on their functioning.  The aim is to reduce executive discretion while strengthening accountability. By creating a common institutional framework for tribunal administration, the Bill seeks to address longstanding concerns over appointments, tenure and functioning, while giving effect to the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in its Madras Bar Association judgments.

Strengthening India’s Tribunal System

The Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026 passed by the Parliament in August 2026, aims to reform the tribunal system to make it more efficient, independent of the executive, transparent and uniform.

The Bill follows various Supreme Court judgements on the independence of tribunals. In Madras Bar Association v. Union of India [(2026) 2 SCC 1], the Supreme Court struck down provisions of the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021. The Court also directed the establishment of an independent National Tribunals Commission.

The 2026 Bill proposes to repeal the Tribunal Reforms Act, 2021. It introduces a new structure to ensure that the system is independent yet accountable to the people it serves.

 

Covered Tribunals & Governing Acts

 

The Bill lists all the Tribunals, Appellate Tribunals, and Authorities governed by the bill, alongside their corresponding Enactments. The changes proposed by the Bill shall apply to these tribunals.

 

Sl. No.

Tribunal / Appellate Tribunal / Authority

Enactments  

1.

Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal

The Customs Act, 1962 (52 of 1962)

2.

Appellate Tribunal

The Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Act, 1976 (13 of 1976)

3.

Central Administrative Tribunal

The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 (13 of 1985)

4.

State Administrative Tribunals

The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 (13 of 1985)

5.

Railway Claims Tribunal

The Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 (54 of 1987)

6.

Securities Appellate Tribunal

The Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (15 of 1992)

7.

Debts Recovery Tribunal

The Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993 (51 of 1993)

8.

Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal

The Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993 (51 of 1993)

9.

Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 (24 of 1997)

10.

Appellate Tribunal for Electricity

The Electricity Act, 2003 (36 of 2003)

11.

Armed Forces Tribunal

The Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007 (55 of 2007)

12.

National Green Tribunal

The National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 (19 of 2010)

13.

National Company Law Appellate Tribunal

The Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013)

14.

National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission

The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)

15.

Industrial Tribunal constituted by the Central Government

The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (35 of 2020)

16.

Income-tax Appellate Tribunal

The Income-tax Act, 2025 (30 of 2025)

 

A New National Tribunals Commission

 

The 2026 Bill aims at protecting the independence of the tribunals system through the establishment of a new National Tribunals Commission (NTC). This commission, which will be dominated by the high-ranking members of the judiciary, replaces the Central Government, which was given the charge of making key appointments and services conditions according to the Tribunal Reforms Act, 2021.

 

Composition of the Commission   

 

The Commission would consist of:

  • A Chairperson who has been a Judge of the Supreme Court or a Chief Justice of a High Court, and
  • Four Members:
    • Two shall be Judicial Members who have been Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court
    • Two shall be Technical Members with at least 25 years of experience in the fields of public administration, finance, law, accountancy, banking, management, or technology.

 

 

 

The Central Government will formally appoint the Chairperson and the Judicial Members of the Commission. However, it must consult the Chief Justice of India before appointing the Chairperson and Judicial Members.

 

Functions of the Commission   

 

Under the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, the National Tribunals Commission (NTC) has several important roles:

  • Conduct selections: Conduct the selection process for filling up the vacancies of Chairpersons and Members of the Tribunals through Search-cum-Selection Committees.
  • Review performance: Monitor tribunal performance and prepares annual reports to be submitted to the Central Government.
  • Oversee inquiries: Supervise inquiries into complaints against tribunal members.
  • Maintain data: Develops and maintains the National Tribunals Data Grid, which is a portal containing the repository of all case-related information pertaining to the 16 tribunals.

 

Term of Service

 

  • The Chairperson of the Commission or a Member of the Commission shall hold office for a term of five years or till he attains the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier
  • A Member of a Tribunal shall hold office for a term of five years or till he attains the age of sixty-seven years, whichever is earlier.

 

The framework also allows reappointment, with previous service and performance considered during the selection process.

 

New Secretariat

 

The Secretariat serves as the administrative support system for the National Tribunals Commission. The Secretariat will be headed by a Secretary to the Government of India. Its other officers and employees, including their number and service conditions, will be prescribed by rules. It will function under the general and administrative oversight of the Commission’s Chairperson. It:

 

  • Empanels experts: Identifies and empanels experts from relevant fields to assess candidates.
  • Communicates recommendations: Sends the Search-cum-Selection Committee’s recommendations to the Central Government within three days.
  • Provides administrative support: Supports the Commission and carries out functions prescribed.
  • Prepares annual reports: Prepares an annual report yearly giving full and true account of the activities of the Commission and forward the report to the Central government.
  •  

Search-cum-Selection Committees

 

The selection of Chairpersons and Members to various tribunals will be done through Search-cum-Selection Committees. These committees will be responsible for evaluating candidates and recommending appointments to tribunal posts.

 

Under Section 13 of the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, the Search-cum-Selection Committee comprises:

For selecting a Tribunal Chairperson

  1. Chairperson of the National Tribunals Commission
  2. Technical Member of the Commission
  3. Retired Chief Justice of a High Court, nominated by the Commission Chairperson
  4. Secretary to the Government of India, nominated by the Central Government. In case of appointment to the post of Chairperson of the State Administrative Tribunals, the Chief Secretary to the State Government concerned shall be the Member
  5. Two empanelled experts who assessed the candidates
  6. Secretary of the Commission — Member Secretary

For selecting a Tribunal Member:

 

  1. Judicial Member of the National Tribunals Commission — Committee Chair
  2. Technical Member of the Commission
  3. Retired High Court Judge, nominated by the Commission Chairperson
  4. Secretary to the Government of India, nominated by the Central Government.  In case of appointment to the post of Member of the State Administrative Tribunals, the Chief Secretary to the State Government concerned shall be the Member
  5. Two empanelled experts who assessed the candidates
  6. Secretary of the Commission — Member Secretary

 

The Committee Chair has the casting vote, while the Member Secretary and expert Members do not have voting rights. The Committee:

 

  • Selects candidates: Conducts the selection process for Chairpersons and Members.
  • Recommends candidates: The Committee recommends one suitable candidate for each vacancy and one additional candidate for the waiting list.
  • Considers past performance: For candidates seeking reappointment, the Committee considers their previous service and performance.
  • Facilitates timely appointments: Recommendations are sent to the Central Government through the Secretariat, which must communicate them within three days. The Government must process the recommendation and make the appointment within three months.

The proposed National Tribunals Commission has a judicial majority. Its Search-cum-Selection Committees are also judicially chaired. The judicial Chairperson has the casting vote. The Committee recommends a single candidate rather than a panel of names. This strengthens judicial influence over the selection process while limiting executive discretion.

 

Financial and Administrative Independence

 

The Bill seeks to give tribunals greater financial and administrative autonomy. Under this framework, individual tribunals will identify their requirements for funds, staff, and premises. The Commission's Secretariat will consolidate these projections, and the Commission will evaluate them using an objective framework to determine overall allocation needs.

The Central Government will continue to allocate the necessary grants following parliamentary appropriation.To ensure financial accountability and transparency, the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG) will audit the accounts of the Commission and forward the audit report to the Central Government, which will then lay it before both Houses of Parliament.

 


 

Towards a More Independent Tribunal System

 

The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026 seeks to establish judicial independence and transparency in the tribunals system. While the Bill reinforces judicial independence, it balances this by keeping the system accountable to the public through parliamentary oversight.

The proposed National Tribunals Commission creates a permanent institutional mechanism for appointments, performance review and disciplinary oversight. Judicially led selection committees strengthen the judicial element in appointments. Expert assessment places greater emphasis on professional competence. Five-year tenure provides greater stability.

The Bill marks a shift from fragmented, executive-driven tribunal rules to a structured institutional framework. Its core goal is to establish a more independent, transparent, and professionally managed system that aligns with the Supreme Court's Madras Bar Association jurisprudence.

2298156.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Fair Trading Practices and Taking ‘Make in India’ from Local to Global
2298156.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Fair Trading Practices and Taking ‘Make in India’ from Local to Global
Nine Free Trade Agreements Open New Market Opportunities for Indian Industry and Businesses: Shri Goyal
India’s $30 Trillion Economy Vision by 2047 Presents Major Opportunities for Businesses: Shri Goyal
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 2:26PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal urged Indian businesses and citizens to adopt fair trading practices, promote recycling and reuse, and encourage a circular economy while taking Indian products and services to global markets.

Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the Bharatiya Vyapar Mahotsav at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, Shri Goyal highlighted India’s growing global economic engagement and noted that markets have been opened for Indian industry and businesses through nine free trade agreements. He said that international trade now provides India preferential access and highlighted the contribution of Indian MSMEs, employees, fishermen, farmers, entrepreneurs and the services sector in taking Indian products and services to global markets.

Shri Goyal called for collective efforts to strengthen the Make in India brand by respecting India’s quality, design capabilities and brand. He said that India’s current economic size of around $4 trillion presents a major opportunity as the country moves towards the vision of becoming a $30 trillion economy by 2047. He noted that the whole world is seeking to increase trade relations with India and emphasised that such a large growth opportunity requires collective participation from businesses, entrepreneurs and citizens.

The Minister noted the growth of India’s exports and said that goods and services exports reached a record level of 863 trillion dollars last year, comprising 442 trillion dollars of merchandise exports and 421 trillion dollars of services exports. He said that exports had registered around 73 per cent growth over the last six years and that the target for the current year is to achieve exports of 1 trillion dollars. He further noted that exports recorded almost 15 per cent growth during the first four months from April to July of the current year.

Shri Goyal emphasised that self-reliance and national development go hand in hand. He said that citizens must themselves become part of the change and contribute to the country’s journey towards self-reliance. He highlighted various initiatives undertaken since 2014, including Digital India, Startup India, Stand-Up India and large-scale infrastructure development, which have contributed to strengthening industry and business and creating opportunities for the youth.

He said that ‘Swadeshi’ represents products made in India with the blood, sweat and tears of Indian citizens. He called upon Indian businesses to move beyond limited markets and take local products and services to global markets. He said that greater participation of Indian consumers in Indian products would create new opportunities, increase production and trade, enable economies of scale and make Indian businesses more competitive.

The Minister said that the people of India have demonstrated their capability to convert challenges into opportunities and emerge stronger. He highlighted the collective strength of travellers, MSMEs, startups, farmers, fishermen, labourers and entrepreneurs and said that this strength would help India take its products and services to the world.

Calling for greater participation in the country’s development journey, Shri Goyal said that the reform process involves improvement, transformation and performance, and that all stakeholders have a responsibility to demonstrate their capabilities and take India to the world through their work.

Shri Goyal called upon businesses and entrepreneurs to digitise their businesses, adopt good manufacturing practices and follow fair trading practices. He emphasised the importance of sustainability in the context of climate change and called for greater focus on recycling, reuse and a circular economy.

The Minister said that India’s journey should not only give a label to Make in India but also establish respect for India’s quality, design capabilities and brand. He expressed confidence that Indian products and natural resources would become trusted globally through these collective efforts.

Shri Goyal also said that growth in GDP would naturally lead to higher production and create employment opportunities. He noted that young people returning to India after completing their education or acquiring new skills through skill development centres would bring new solutions to address emerging challenges.

He emphasised that the collective efforts of Indian businesses, entrepreneurs, MSMEs, farmers, fishermen and workers would contribute to the country’s growth and help India emerge as a stronger participant in the global economy.

2298148.title: National AI Skilling Initiative Records 60,253 Enrolments in Phase I; IICT and Private Sector Partners have Jointly Developed Curriculum to Equip Students with Industry-Relevant AI Skills
2298148.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
National AI Skilling Initiative Records 60,253 Enrolments in Phase I; IICT and Private Sector Partners have Jointly Developed Curriculum to Equip Students with Industry-Relevant AI Skills
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 2:10PM by PIB Delhi

The total number of applications received, and participants enrolled under Phase I of the National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Skilling Initiative as on date is 60,253.

The total number of participants who have completed 2 Modules of Phase I of the programme are 4620 and those who have completed all 4 Modules of Phase I of the programme are 552.

Phase I of the programme comprises four modules with a total duration of 33 hours, delivered through two learning platforms. The details of the Modules of Phase I are as under: -

Platform 1:

  • Module 1: AI Essentials – gain practical skills to boost daily productivity, synthesize data, and create content.
  • Module 2: Prompting Essentials – framework to write professional prompts.

Platform 2:

  • Module 3: Introduction to Generative AI – grasp Large Language Model (LLM) fundamentals and responsible AI guidelines.
  • Module 4: Generative AI Leader – master workflow automation and strategic Gen AI organisational transformation.

The details of Phase II, including the curriculum, modules and course duration, are under finalisation.

The curriculum has been jointly designed and developed by the IICT and private sector partners to impart foundational and practical AI skills. The advanced skilling component is conducted by IICT for joint certification.

The Government’s role has been to provide strategic direction and facilitating the implementation of the programme through IICT with the objective of enhancing AI literacy and equipping students with industry-relevant digital skills.

The information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to a Question asked by Adv Gowaal Kagada Padavi in Lok Sabha today.

2298141.title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: MISSION KARMAYOGI
2298141.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2298141.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: MISSION KARMAYOGI
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 2:04PM by PIB Delhi

Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) was approved by the Government of India in September 2020 with an aim of transitioning from a 'rule- based' to 'role-based' HR system and creating civil servants with a global outlook while being rooted in Indian ethos.

The iGOT Karmayogi digital learning portal, established under the Mission Karmayogi, has continued to expand rapidly in scale and reach. The portal, currently, has more than 1.7 crore registered users. It hosts more than 5,600 courses across domain, functional, and behavioural competencies, covering a total of 6,953 hours of learning. Courses are available in 23 languages, including English and Hindi, enabling wide accessibility and alignment with regional and linguistic needs. There have been more than 14.42 crore course completions on iGOT so far.

To strengthen continuous capacity building and digital learning across all levels of government, employees from Central Government, States/UTs, as well as urban and rural local bodies have been onboarded on iGOT. To ensure role-based training, Capacity Building Plans are being made for all Ministries, Departments, and Organisations (MDOs). The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), along with the Capacity Building Commission (CBC) and SPV Karmayogi Bharat (KB) continuously monitors the progress and provides necessary support to all stakeholders in this regard. Government employees are also nudged and encouraged towards digital learning, and spirit of continuous learning is promoted through special initiatives like the National Learning Week - Karmayogi Saptah (held in October 2024) and the SADHANA Saptah (April 2026).

This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2298140.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2298140.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: STRENGTHENING OF CPGRAMS
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 2:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has undertaken several measures to strengthen the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS). Major reforms include adoption of next-generation technologies to enhance system capabilities, introduction of the Grievance Redressal Assessment and Index (GRAI) to benchmark the performance of Ministries and Departments, publication of monthly CPGRAMS reports for transparency and monitoring, capacity building of grievance officers through Sevottam, integration with the grievance portals of Central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs, multilingual grievance registration and translation facility through integration with Bhashini, operationalization of the Feedback Call Centre, availability of CPGRAMS through the mobile application and Common Service Centres (CSCs), reduction of prescribed grievance disposal timeline from 30 days to 21 days, and launch of 'Samadhan Didi', an AI-powered multilingual voice-first chatbot for grievance registration.

 

Further, to improve the quality of grievance redressal, the Comprehensive Guidelines on Handling of Public Grievances, issued in August 2024, mandates establishment of dedicated Grievance Cells in Ministries/Departments, appointment of experienced nodal officers, monitoring of pendency and citizen feedback, emphasis on root cause analysis, and strengthened escalation mechanisms. In addition, a dedicated Review Meeting Module has been operationalised in CPGRAMS to facilitate senior-level review of public grievances to further improve the efficiency and quality of grievance redressal.

2298116.title: Government Expands Citizen-Centric Digital Public Service Delivery through UMANG and DigiLocker
2298116.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Government Expands Citizen-Centric Digital Public Service Delivery through UMANG and DigiLocker
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 1:40PM by PIB Delhi

In line with the Hon'ble Prime Minister's vision to democratise technology and empower citizens, the Government of India launched the Digital India programme in July 2015. Under the Digital India programme, the Government has undertaken several initiatives to improve digital access and ensure seamless citizen-centric service delivery including UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) and DigiLocker platforms.

As on 31st July 2026, approximately 2,575 services [Central Government: 880; State Government: 1695] across India are available on the UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) platform, and 5,437 document types/services [Central Government: 661; State Government: 4,776] are available on DigiLocker platform.

UMANG has more than 11.66 Crore registered users witnessing about 798 Crore transactions in the last 3 years, and DigiLocker has more than 72.43 Crore registered users and has about 72.86 Crore document access transactions in the last 3 years.

The Government has expanded the network of Common Service Centres (CSCs) to improve digital access in rural and remote areas. CSCs provide citizen-centric digital services. These include government, banking, financial, insurance, pension and utility payment services. As on 30 June 2026, 4,07,122 CSCs were functional at the Gram Panchayat level. Of these, 70,069 CSCs were operated by women Village Level Entrepreneurs.

Other key measures to improve digital access and ensure seamless service delivery in rural, remote, and underserved regions are as below:

 

  • Mobile and Web-based Access: Both UMANG and DigiLocker platforms are available through mobile applications and web portals, enabling citizens to access Government services anytime and anywhere.
  • Integration with Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI): UMANG and DigiLocker is integrated with key Digital Public Infrastructure components such as Aadhaar, eSign, API Setu, and other major digital platforms, enabling seamless and paperless service delivery.
  • Secure and Paperless Governance: Both platforms provide secure authentication, digital document verification and consent-based sharing, reducing the need for physical visits and paper-based processes while ensuring efficient service delivery.
  • Digital Literacy and Awareness: The Government promotes digital literacy through initiatives such as PMGDISHA (Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan) and conducts awareness campaigns to encourage the use of digital platforms.
  • Multilingual and Accessible Services: UMANG and DigiLocker offers services in multiple Indian languages and continuously improves accessibility and user experience to make digital services more inclusive.
  • Continuous Expansion of Services: Government Departments and State Governments are regularly onboarded to integrate more citizen-centric services and digital documents on UMANG and DigiLocker.

 

This statement was given by the Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in Rajya Sabha on 07-08-2026.

The Startup Accelerator of MeitY for Product Innovation, Development, and Growth (SAMRIDH) programme, designed to accelerate around 300 Startups through existing and upcoming Accelerators in Health-tech, Ed-tech, Agri-tech, Consumer-tech, Fin-tech, Software as a Service (SaaS) and sustainability sectors. The programme successfully concluded on 31st January, 2026.

During the last five years, 7 accelerators from the State of Andhra Pradesh submitted Expressions of Interest (EoI) under the SAMRIDH programme. The SAMRIDH programme provides financial support of ₹2 lakh per startup to selected accelerators, along with matching funding to startups up to a maximum of ₹40 lakh, in accordance with programme guidelines. 2298108.title: Government Promotes Sustainable Growth of Data Centres through Energy-Efficient and Clean Energy Measures
2298108.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Government Promotes Sustainable Growth of Data Centres through Energy-Efficient and Clean Energy Measures
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 1:37PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision, the Government is democratising the development and usage of technology.

 

Data centres are an important & integral component of the overall Digital India Infrastructure ecosystem. The Data Centre industry in India has been growing at a steady pace. The rapid growth of AI and high-performance computing is driving increasing demand for data centre capacity in the country.

 

Data centres are located across the country majorly in areas such as Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR and Jamnagar. The installed capacity has grown from 375 MW in 2020 to current capacity of about 1575 MW.

 

The Data Centre industry is now further expanding in States like Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh & West Bengal which are coming up as new investment destinations.

 

The current data centres capacity across the country is less than 1% of the current installed power capacity. As per Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Ministry of Power (MoP), the power demand of data centres is estimated to be about 17 GW up to 2031-32.

 

Energy Efficiency & Water Conservation

  • The Government of India is promoting renewable energy through measures such as Green Energy Open Access Rules, Green Energy Corridor Scheme, Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM), National Green Hydrogen Mission, National Programme on High Efficiency Solar PV Modules, Offshore Wind VGF Scheme and Solar Park Scheme.
  • Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, has been enacted to strengthen reliable clean power for emerging sectors such as AI and data centres, including future deployment of Small Modular and Micro Nuclear Reactors.
  • Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), through technical committee LITD 31 (Cloud Computing, IT & Data Centres), has published a series of Indian Standards on Power Usage Effectiveness, Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE), Cooling Efficiency Ratio (CER), Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) related to data centres.
  • The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) has notified Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC 2017) and Energy Conservation & Sustainable Building Code (ECSBC 2024) prescribing energy efficiency and water conservation norms for buildings, including provisions relevant to data centres.
  • The water requirement of data centres depends on the type of cooling technologies deployed. Regulation and control of groundwater extraction, including for industrial purposes, is governed by the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. With the advancement of AI infrastructure, data centre cooling systems are also adopting advanced technologies such as direct-to-chip liquid cooling, adiabatic cooling, immersion cooling and closed-loop liquid cooling systems.

 

Industry is also deploying high density racks to efficiently support high‑performance computing & AI workloads for further reduction of power and water consumption.

 

These initiatives collectively provide a framework for electricity consumption and energy efficiency, renewable energy use, energy reuse, cooling efficiency, carbon emissions and water usage.

 

This information was submitted by Union Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada in Rajya Sabha on 07.08.2026.

2298105.title: HOLISTIC DEVELOPMENT OF FISHERIES
2298105.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2298105.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
HOLISTIC DEVELOPMENT OF FISHERIES
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi

The fisheries sector is one of the fastest-growing agri-allied sectors in the country and plays a significant role in economic growth, food and nutritional securities, employment generation, livelihood support and export earnings. Under entry 21 of List-II of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India – “Fisheries” is within the purview of the State Governments. Whereas under entry 57 of List-I of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India – “Fishing and fisheries beyond territorial waters” is within the mandate of the Union of India. The fisheries sector, during 2023-24 has contributed about 7.43% to the Agricultural Gross Value Added (GVA) and about 1.09% to the country's total GVA.

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has taken up several steps for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector including welfare of fishers and fish farmers in the country. The steps taken up include implementation of fisheries and aquaculture development schemes such as (i) Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), (ii) Fisheries & Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), (iii) Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY). In addition, the Government of India with effect from the financial year 2018-19 has extended the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish famers to help them to meet their working capital requirements.

The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) implemented by the DoF, GoI inter-alia provides for one-time incentive for purchase of aquaculture insurance by farmers. The one-time incentive for aquaculture insurance is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹25,000 per hectare, or ₹1 lakh per farmer for 4 hectares Water Spread Area (WSA). For the aquaculture system including intensive systems like farms, cage culture, Recirculatory Aquaculture System (RAS), bio-floc and raceways, aquaculture insurance is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹1 lakh per farmer for 1800 m3 intensive aquaculture systems. Further, the SC/ST and women beneficiaries get an additional 10% of the incentive given to the General Category Farmers.

This Information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.

2298106.title: PMMSY IN CHHATTISGARH
2298106.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2298106.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
PMMSY IN CHHATTISGARH
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been implementing the flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total outlay of Rs. 20,750 crore from 2020-21 to 2026-27 (September, 2026) for the sustainable development of fisheries and aquaculture in all the States and Union Territories including Chhattisgarh. The PMMSY scheme has significantly contributed to the development of the fisheries sector in Chhattisgarh by enhancing the financial, social, and economic security of fishermen and fish farmers through infrastructure, production, aquaculture expansion, technology infusion, support for welfare activities, market expansion and welfare interventions.

The Department of Fisheries, Government of India accorded approvals to projects under PMMSY worth Rs. 956.86 crore with a central share of Rs. 321.01 crore to Government of Chhattisgarh during last six years (2020-21 to 2025-26). Out of the approved central share, an amount of Rs. 274.16 crore was released to Government of Chhattisgarh in the last six years (2020-21 to 2025-26). In order to enhance the financial, social and economic security of fishermen, the major projects approved under PMMSY to the State are  28 numbers of Fish Seed Hatcheries, 3200 hectares of New Fish Ponds, 287 numbers of Re-circulatory Aquaculture System, 820 numbers Biofloc units, 14 nos. of Fish Feed Mills of various capacities, 511 numbers of Small Fish Transport Vehicles, 8500 Cages in Reservoirs and one Integrated Aqua Park (IAP) along with social security measures such as accidental insurance coverage of 5.52 lakh fishers annually, Livelihood and Nutritional support to 9667 fishers annually and improved access to institutional credit to 4189 fishers through the Kisan Credit Card (KCC). Collectively, these interventions have enhanced fish production (from 3.14 lakh metric tonnes in 2014-15 to 8.73 lakh metric tonnes in 2024-25), increased farmers' incomes, promoted entrepreneurship, generated rural employment, reduced post-harvest losses, and contributed to the overall socio-economic development of the fisheries sector in Chhattisgarh.

This Information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.

2298104.title: PROBLEMS FACED BY AQUA FARMERS
2298104.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2298104.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
PROBLEMS FACED BY AQUA FARMERS
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 1:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of Andhra Pradesh has informed that as per data recorded on the e‑Fish platform and as per the database maintained by the State Government, approximately 2.16 lakh aquaculture farmers are engaged in aquaculture activities in the State, covering about 5.79 lakh acres under freshwater and brackish water aquaculture. 

As reported by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, aqua farmers in the State are facing difficulties due to the decline in market prices and increase in the cost of fish feed. The Government of Andhra Pradesh has taken various measures to address the issue, including initiatives to reduce feed cost. In this regard, feed manufacturers have agreed to reduce the price of shrimp feed by Rs.4.00 per kilogram.

The Government of Andhra Pradesh has informed that the State Fisheries Department is actively coordinating with aqua farmers’ associations, value-added enterprises, exporters and other stakeholders to address the issues faced by fish and shrimp farmers. It has also been informed by the State Government that no State-wide crop holiday has been officially implemented.

The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, in coordination with the Government of Andhra Pradesh, is taking various measures to safeguard the interests of aqua farmers in the State. As informed by the State Government, registered aqua farmers are being provided electricity at a subsidised tariff of ₹1.50 per unit. Further, through consultations with feed manufacturers, the price of shrimp feed in the State has been reduced by ₹4.00 per kilogram. Recognising the importance of improving the economic viability of shrimp farming, the Government of India has undertaken several policy measures to reduce the cost of aquaculture production. In the Union Budgets 2024–25 and 2025–26, customs duties on 16 key aquaculture inputs were rationalised, with rates reduced from 30% to as low as 0–5%, thereby lowering the cost of essential inputs. Further, in September 2025, the Government of India approved the reduction of GST rates from 12–18% to 5% on more than 20 fisheries and aquaculture‑related products, including farm equipment, feed ingredients, water conditioners, fishing nets and value‑added seafood products.

These measures are expected to reduce production costs, improve the profitability of farmers across various States, including Andhra Pradesh, and enhance the competitiveness of India’s aquaculture sector. In addition, the Government of India and the State Government are promoting value‑added enterprises to minimise post‑harvest losses and augment the income of fish farmers.

This Information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.

2298102.title: PROTECTION OF TRADITIONAL FISHING RIGHTS AND LIVELIHOODS
2298102.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2298102.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
PROTECTION OF TRADITIONAL FISHING RIGHTS AND LIVELIHOODS
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 1:33PM by PIB Delhi

The fisheries up to 12 nautical miles from baseline is governed by the coastal States in accordance with their Marine Fishing Regulation Acts (MFRAs). Under the respective MFRAs, many coastal States/UTs have reserved fishing zones for different categories of fishing vessels. Near-shore coastal waters, generally up to 5 to 10 kilometers from the shore, are exclusively reserved for artisanal and non-mechanized traditional fishing vessels, which protects traditional livelihoods, minimizes gear conflicts, and prevents resource overexploitation. Joint patrolling is conducted by State Fisheries Departments along with enforcement agencies, including the Indian Coast Guard (ICG), to prevent incursion of mechanised fishing vessels into such reserved zones. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), satellite‑based transponders are installed on mechanized and motorized fishing vessels, enabling real‑time vessel tracking with geofencing and automated alerts to authorities in cases of incursion into areas reserved for traditional fishers.

The concept of Blue Economy encompasses many sub-sectors, including fisheries. Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt of India, is steering the draft National Policy for India’s Blue Economy. Sagarmala is a central sector scheme of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways with the target to promote port-led development in the country. As part of the project development, the respective project proponents are required to prepare the Social and Environmental Impact Assessment Report to assess the potential impacts of the proposed projects on the community and the environment. Simultaneously, project proponents need to prepare and implement a Social and Environmental Management Plan to mitigate any negative impacts that emerge during the studies of baseline conditions, impact assessment, and evaluation for the project. Further, improvement in the livelihood of communities in coastal areas is also undertaken through implementation of projects identified under the coastal community development pillar of the Sagarmala Scheme.

The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) being the nodal Ministry, reviews the issues relating to Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notifications issued from time to time. MoEF&CC, based on suggestions and proposals received from various stakeholders of coastal States/UTs, reviews the CRZ Notification for development of infrastructure along the coast, including concerns of the fishermen community.

The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI), has undertaken comprehensive measures towards sustainable harnessing of marine fisheries resources and the welfare of small-scale and traditional fishers. The Government has notified the Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Rules, 2025 that mandates key conservation measures, including ecosystem approach to fisheries management, implementation of the uniform ban on fishing during fish breeding seasons; minimum legal size for fish capture and adoption of bycatch reduction measures, prohibition of destructive and juvenile fishing practices, and promotion of best practices to minimize post-harvest losses.

To ensure sustainable fishing, enhance fish stocks, and safety of fishermen at sea, a uniform 61‑day annual fishing ban is implemented in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of India during the peak fish breeding season. Coastal States/UTs also enforce a corresponding ban within their territorial waters, aligning their schedules with the uniform ban notified by the DoF, GoI. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), livelihood and nutritional support is provided to socio‑economically backward active traditional fishers’ families during the fishing ban/lean period. PMMSY also extends coverage through a Group Accidental Insurance Scheme for active fishers, ensuring social security and risk protection during fishing operations.

Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), the Government of India has, for the first time, extended dedicated support for sea ranching and installation of Artificial Reefs along the country’s coastline. These interventions help prevent habitat degradation, enhance fish stocks, and strengthen the livelihoods of coastal fishers. PMMSY also promotes mariculture activities, including seaweed cultivation and open‑sea cage culture, to reduce fishing pressure in nearshore waters and sustainably augment marine fisheries production. PMMSY further includes the component “Development of 100 Coastal Fishermen Villages as Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV)”, aimed at transforming 100 villages selected jointly with the coastal States/UTs into economically vibrant and climate‑resilient villages through need-based interventions including infrastructure and livelihood‑enhancing activities.

This Information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.

2298101.title: SALIENT FEATURE OF PM-MKSSY
2298101.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2298101.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
SALIENT FEATURE OF PM-MKSSY
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been implementing a Central Sector Sub-scheme namely the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) under the ongoing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for a period of four years from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27 at an estimated outlay of Rs.6000 crore. The National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) was launched under PM-MKSSY on 11.09.2024 to extend digital services. The salient features of the sub-scheme are (i) Gradual formalization of the unorganized fisheries sector including creation of work based digital identities of fish workers for improved service delivery, (ii) Facilitating greater access to institutional finance including working capital in order to enable the fish farmers, fishers and micro and small enterprises to reduce their capital cost and to expand their operations (iii) Strengthening fisheries cooperatives by enhancing their institutional capacity, improving market access, facilitating access to finance, and business development plans and need based support (iv) Providing one-time incentive to the fish farmers for purchase of aquaculture insurance, (v) Incentivizing fisheries and aquaculture microenterprises to improve value-chain efficiencies and to create and maintain jobs through performance grants, (vi) Incentivizing micro and small enterprises in the fisheries sector to establish supply chains of safe fish and fishery products including creation and maintenance of jobs through performance grants.

The PM-MKSSY under its component 1-B provides for one-time incentive for purchase of aquaculture insurance by farmers.  The one-time incentive for aquaculture insurance is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹25,000 per hectare, or ₹1 lakh per farmer for 4 hectares Water Spread Area (WSA). For the aquaculture system including intensive systems like farms, cage culture, RAS, bio-floc, and raceways etc. the incentive is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹1 lakh per farmer for 1800 m3. Further, the SC/ST and women beneficiaries get an additional 10% of incentive given to the general category.

 The PM-MKSSY promotes environmentally sustainable and climate-resilient fisheries and aquaculture by incentivizing projects adopting decarbonization, improved energy and water-use efficiency, use of renewable energy, climate-smart technologies, improved hygiene and waste/pollution management, reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, sustainable production practices, and Better Management Practices including disease management, waste management, quality and safety standards, certification, traceability etc..

The PM-MKSSY supports for improvement of fisheries value-chain efficiencies and establishment of supply chains of safe fish products to consumers under Components 2 and 3 through Performance Grant for Microenterprises at the rate of  25% of the total investment or Rs.35 lakhs, whichever is lower, for General Category and 35% of total investment or Rs.45 lakhs, whichever is lower, for SC, ST and Women owned microenterprises. In addition, Performance Grant for Village Level Organizations and Federations of SHGs, FFPOs and Cooperatives shall not exceed 35% of total investment or Rs.200 lakhs, whichever is lower. Within the limit of the Performance Grant, the PM-MKSSY provides an amount of Rs.10,000 and Rs.15,000 per year for creation and maintenance of jobs for men and woman respectively subject to the limit of 50% of total eligible Performance Grant. In addition, the PM-MKSSY, inter alia, promotes Indian seafood exports through support for quality and sustainable aquaculture, value addition, certification, traceability, disease surveillance, and modern post-harvest and cold-chain infrastructure, food safety and quality assurance with a view to enhancing global competitiveness and value realisation. The scheme also supports fisheries micro and small enterprises for adoption of improved technologies, processing, packaging, and market linkages across the fisheries value chain.

Further, the PM-MKSSY is a demand-driven Sub-Scheme and implemented in all the States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh. There are no district-specific interventions or district-wise or State-wise employment targets including in Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh. However, the scheme aims to generate 1.70 lakh jobs.

This Information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.

2298098.title: ACCESS PASS FOR FISHING IN INDIA'S EEZ
2298098.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2298098.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
ACCESS PASS FOR FISHING IN INDIA'S EEZ
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 1:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Access Pass for fishing in India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), is a free digital pass issued via the ReALCRaft Portal. Its core objective is to empower the traditional fishers, cooperatives, and Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) for fishing in the EEZ (12 to 200 nautical miles), while ensuring sustainability of oceanic fishery resources. The Access Pass is issued under the Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Rules, 2025 notified by the Government of India on 04 November 2025. The Access Pass is required for mechanized fishing vessels and large motorized boats over 24 meters length, while traditional non-motorized and small artisanal crafts are fully exempted to protect local livelihoods. This landmark initiative aims to empower traditional and small-scale fishermen, Fisheries Cooperative Societies, and Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) to expand fishing operations, harness untapped resources through deep-sea fishing, and access new income streams through processing and exports, thereby enhancing livelihoods. As per the EEZ Rules, the Access Pass is required for undertaking fishing operations in the EEZ of India, beyond 12 nautical miles. So far, a total of 9,650 Access Passes have been issued based on applications received through coastal States and Union Territories. The State/UT‑wise status of Access Passes issued under the EEZ Rules, 2025 is placed at Annexure.

To create new export opportunities for Indian fishers operating beyond territorial waters, the Union Budget 2026–27 announced that fish caught by Indian fishing vessels in the EEZ or the High Seas would be duty‑free, and that landings at foreign ports would be treated as exports of goods, with safeguards to prevent misuse during transit or transshipment. In pursuance of this announcement, necessary amendments have been carried out in the Customs Act, 1962 to ensure that the fish caught in the EEZ is duty‑free. The Access Pass issued through ReALCRaft portal, is linked with the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) and the Export Inspection Council (EIC) to provide seamless catch and health certificates, to ensure traceability and eco-labelling.

  Adopting a whole‑of‑Government approach, the Department of Fisheries, GoI is collaborating with the Ministry of Cooperation through a Joint Working Group (JWG) to promote small‑scale fishermen, fisheries cooperatives, and FFPOs in deep‑sea fishing, post‑harvest handling, processing, and exports. The Ministry of Cooperation supports this initiative by strengthening cooperative institutions and facilitating access to cooperative credit through the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), the NCDC has supported for acquisition of Deep‑Sea Fishing Vessels in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Puducherry and Goa. The NCDC has also supported the acquisition of Deep‑Sea Fishing Vessels under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) implemented by DoF, GoI.

The Access Pass framework operates in convergence with the existing digital fisheries and maritime safety systems. It is integrated with satellite‑based transponders installed onboard Fishing Vessels and linked with the Nabhmitra mobile application to provide real-time advisories of Potential-Fishing-Zone (PFZ), dissemination of weather forecasts, cyclone and tsunami warnings, navigational advisories, International Maritime Boundary Line (IMBL) alerts, emergency communication, and other safety‑related information delivered directly to fishers at sea for enhancing safety and improving fishing efficiency.

2298081.title: “DBT Tribal Portal and Tribal Scholarship Disbursement”
2298081.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
“DBT Tribal Portal and Tribal Scholarship Disbursement”
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 12:44PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed Rajya Sabha that currently, the Ministry is already leveraging the benefit of DBT Tribal Portal by accessing the data of beneficiaries submitted by the respective State/UT for monitoring and generating MIS reports for the implementation of pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes. The States/UTs have also been given facilities to upload queries, documents, utilization certificates, statement of expenditure etc. which has reduced processing time and reduced grievances. The details of the number of beneficiaries reported by the States/UTs on the DBT Tribal Portal for the pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes during the last three financial years are given at Annexure-I.

The Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes are the Centrally Sponsored Schemes and implemented through respective States/UTs. The disbursement of scholarships is carried out by the concerned State/UT through their own portal or NSP portal. The progress made through the Portal are given as under: -

  1. End-to-End Digitization: Transition from paper-based processing to scheme-specific digital portals.
  2. Common Data Standard: Implementation of standard data format for seamless web-service API based data sharing between States/UT portals/ National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and the DBT Tribal Portal of the Ministry
  3. Faster Communication and Online Processing: Online upload of Utilization Certificates (UCs), Statements of Expenditure (SoE), and queries by States, significantly reducing processing time and administrative delays.
  4. Public Transparency & Outcome Dashboards: Integration of beneficiary and transaction data with the Performance Dashboard of the Ministry, DBT Mission, Prayas Dashboard, and NITI Aayog for outcome tracking.

 

The data of beneficiaries reported by the State/UTs in the DBT Tribal Portal have been useful for monitoring and generating MIS reports. Integration of National Scholarship Portal with States/UTs scholarship portal enables data validation and automated deduplication checks across schemes and databases.

Under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for ST students, to eliminate parking of funds at State level, minimize delays in release of scholarship, and ensure transparency of fund flow, the Ministry has adopted the SNA SPARSH Model for release of central share under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme. This serves as a Just-in-Time Disbursement Framework under which the Central Share funds are release in "Just-in-time" as and when the bills are raised by respective State Govt for payment of scholarship. Once the bills for scholarship payment is approved, both Central Share as well as State Share fund is directly transferred from RBI account to Student beneficiary account on through DBT. This eliminates the parking of central share funds at state level and minimize delay in disbursement of scholarship.

Under Central Sector Schemes of Scholarship implemented directly by the Ministry, a robust digital mechanism is established through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP), Ministry’s Scholarship Portal and the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) to facilitate Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

Removal of physical application process and manual verification by Institute/District/State authorities has streamlined approval workflows and reduced the overall application processing time. Transfer of Scholarship amount through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the beneficiary student bank accounts ensures that financial benefit reaches targeted ST students in time and without involvement of intermediaries.

National Overseas Scholarship for ST students (NOS)

Under the NOS (National Overseas Scholarship) scheme for ST students, no students from the State of Tamil Nadu were selected in the last three years.

 

The details of the major schemes being implemented by M/o Tribal Affairs are as under:

i. Pre-Matric Scholarships to ST students: The scheme is applicable to students who are studying in Classes IX –X. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Scholarship of Rs.225/-per month for day scholars and Rs.525/-per month for hostellers is given for a period of 10 months in a year. Scholarship is disbursed through the State Government/UT Administration. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except North East and Hills States/UT like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10.For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share.

 

ii. Post Matric Scholarship to ST students: The objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the Scheduled Tribe students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary levels to enable them to complete their education. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Compulsory fees charged by educational institutions are reimbursed subject to the limit fixed by the concerned State Fee fixation committee and scholarship amount of Rs.230 to Rs.1200 per month, depending upon the course of study is paid. The Scheme is implemented by the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except NE and Hilly States/UT of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10. For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share.

National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students: This a Central Sector Schemes implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. The scheme has two sub-Schemes, viz:

 

iii. a National Scholarship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students (earlier known as Top Class Scholarship Scheme): Under this Scheme, Scholarship is provided for pursuing Graduate/Post Graduate courses in the selected top-class Government and Non-Government Institutes in professional fields such as Management, Medicine, Engineering, Information Technology, Law etc. All the ST students, with annual parental income is not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs and studying in the 265 notified institutes by the Ministry, are eligible to receive scholarship. This scheme is started from year 2007 - 08.

b. National Fellowship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students: It is a Central Sector Scheme, fully

funded by Ministry of Tribal Affairs to grant scholarship to meritorious ST students for pursuing Ph.D in India after completion of Master degree. This scheme is started from year 2005-06. The total number of fresh fellowships for Ph.D every year will be 750. ST students with a minimum of 55% marks in Master Degree up to the age of 36 years are eligible to apply for fellowship under the Scheme. The value of fellowship is at par with UGC rates.

 

iv. National Overseas Scholarship for ST students: It is a Central Sector Scheme of Ministry of Tribal Affairs under which scholarships are given to the meritorious Schedule Tribe (ST) students for pursuing higher education in top 1000 ranked (as per latest QS world ranking) Institutes/Universities abroad. This scheme is started from year 1954-55. The Scheme is implemented through the Indian Embassies/Missions abroad, Ministry of External Affairs. Twenty awards are given every year. ST students with annual family income not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs are eligible to apply for the Scholarship under the Scheme.

 

v. Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan: Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) on 2nd October, 2024. The Abhiyan comprises of 25 interventions implemented by 17-line Ministries and aims to saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages, provide social infrastructure like hostels, Anganwadi facilities and mobile medical units and set up Van Dhan Vikas Kendras to provide livelihood opportunities benefiting more than 5 crore tribals in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks in 30 States/UTs in 5 years. The Abhiyan has a total budgetary outlay of Rs.79,156 Cr (Central share: ₹56,333 Cr and State share: ₹22,823 Cr).

 

vi. Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN): Government launched Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) for socio-economic development of 75 PVTG communities residing in 18 states and one UT. The mission aims to provide basic facilities such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities in 3 years. These objectives are planned to be met through 11 interventions including Hostels and Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) implemented by 9-line Ministries. PM JANMAN has total budgetary outlay of Rs.24,104 Cr (Central share: ₹15336 Cr and State share: ₹8768 Cr).

 

vii. Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution: Under the Proviso to Article 275(1) of Constitution, Grants are released to States, having ST population for raising the level of administration in Scheduled Areas and for the welfare of tribal people. This is a Special Area Programme and 100% grants are provided to States. Funds are released to the State Governments depending on the felt needs of ST population to bridge the gap in infrastructure activities in the fields of education, health, skill development, livelihood, drinking water, sanitation, etc.

 

viii. Grant-in Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes: Under the scheme of Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes, the Ministry funds projects in the fields of education and health, covering residential schools, non-residential schools, hostels, mobile dispensaries, ten or more bedded hospitals, livelihood, etc.

 

ix. Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS): The Scheme provides quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe students in remote and tribal areas with the objective of enabling them to access quality education comparable to the best institutions in the country. The schools provide modern educational infrastructure along with facilities for holistic development of tribal students. Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the Central Sector Scheme of EMRS for providing quality education to tribal students, both boys and girls, in their own environment; the EMRSs are to be at par with Navodaya Vidyalayas, with special facilities for preserving local art and culture besides providing training in sports and skill development.

 

x. Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM): The Mission promotes sustainable livelihoods of Scheduled Tribes through value addition, entrepreneurship development, marketing support and strengthening of tribal producer organisations, with emphasis on value chains based on Minor Forest Produce and other tribal products.

 

xi. Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK): Van Dhan Vikas Kendras are set up under the Minimum Support Price for Minor Forest Produce scheme, implemented through TRIFED, for value addition and livelihood support to Minor Forest Produce gatherers.

 

xii. Tribal Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-ECE): The Scheme supports Tribal Research Institutes for research, documentation, capacity building, preservation and promotion of tribal culture, awareness generation, information dissemination and evidence-based policy support.

 

xiii. Monitoring, Evaluation, Survey and Social Audit (MESSA): The Scheme supports monitoring, evaluation, impact assessment, surveys and social audit of programmes implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to strengthen evidence-based planning, policy formulation and effective implementation of tribal development initiatives.

 

 

 

xiv. Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST): The Scheme is implemented through the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) to provide concessional venture capital assistance to Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs for establishment and expansion of income-generating enterprises.

 

xv. National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC): under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is an apex organisation set up exclusively for economic development of Scheduled Tribes implements various schemes for livelihood generation. NSTFDC extends concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe communities.

These measures help to improve access to education, healthcare, livelihoods and connectivity for tribal communities in Tamil Nadu. These include PMS, PMS, NFHEST, NOS, EMRS and hostels for ST boys and girls to promote education. Healthcare services are strengthened through MMUs and Ayush Wellness Centres in PVTG habitations under PM-JANMAN, and through health and nutrition camps organised under DAJGUA. Livelihood support is provided through VDVKs, PMJVM, term loans, micro-credit and skill development through NSTFDC, DAPST, and convergence with MGNREGA, PM Vishwakarma and PM-KISAN under DAJGUA. Connectivity in tribal areas is being improved through provision of all-weather roads, electrification and telecom connectivity under PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA in convergence with the Ministry of Rural Development, State Governments and other implementing agencies.

(c): The physical and financial progress of tribal development schemes, including those in Tamil Nadu, is monitored on a continuous basis through the STCMIS portal for Ministry schemes, the PM-JANMAN Dashboard on the PM Gati Shakti portal for real-time habitation-wise monitoring in convergence with the concerned Ministries, regular review meetings with State Governments/UT Administrations on PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA, and periodic assessment of socio-economic indicators of Scheduled Tribes through the Population Census, NFHS and third-party evaluation studies commissioned by the Ministry to assess outcomes and improve programme implementation. 2298077.title: Cultural identity, language and traditional rights of Scheduled Tribes
2298077.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Cultural identity, language and traditional rights of Scheduled Tribes
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 12:42PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed Rajya Sabha that to preserve, document and promote tribal heritage, including tribal art forms, languages, oral traditions and indigenous knowledge systems, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides financial assistance to 29 Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs), including the Tribal Research Institute, Jharkhand, under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme "Support to Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs)". TRIs function under the administrative control of the respective State Governments/UT Administrations and implement approved Annual Action Plans with financial support from the Ministry. The TRI, Jharkhand undertakes activities such as documentation of tribal languages, folklore, customs and traditional knowledge, organisation of cultural programmes, strengthening of tribal museums and publication of research. The Ministry has also developed digital initiatives for documentation and showcasing tribal cultural resources from Jharkhand through TribeX (erstwhile Adi Sanskriti) digital platform for the preservation and promotion of tribal heritage. Under the Ministry's TribeX initiative, the tribal art forms of Jharkhand, namely Sohrai Painting, Dokra Craft, and Jadupetia Chitrakar, have been included as short-term certificate courses. Further, the Ministry also developed AI based translation tool “Adi Vaani” which supports the preservation and wider accessibility of Jharkhand's tribal languages, including Santhali and Mundari, through AI-enabled text and speech translation between tribal languages and Hindi/English.

The implementation of constitutional safeguards and statutory provisions relating to Scheduled Areas, including the provisions of the Fifth Schedule to the Constitution, the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) and the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, is primarily the responsibility of the State Government. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides policy guidance, advisories and capacity-building support, while Tribal Research Institutes undertake research, studies and documentation to support evidence-based policy formulation and effective implementation.

Financial assistance is provided by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to Tribal Research Institutes under the scheme "Support to Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs)" for approved activities relating to research, documentation, preservation and promotion of tribal culture, establishment and strengthening of tribal museums, training, publications and dissemination of tribal knowledge. Funds are released to the State Government/Tribal Research Institute based on approved Annual Action Plans, availability of funds and fulfilment of prescribed conditions. Assistance is not released as a separate component exclusively for tribal cultural preservation. Details of the projects/activities sanctioned to Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) are available on the Ministry’s portal: https://tribal.nic.in/Display_Apex_Minutes.aspx

As on date, no such proposal is under consideration of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
